full_text:
It began with a gardener being hired to trim grass at a harbourside mansion in Sydney – and escalated to payments being left in a shoe for the unlawful felling of hundreds of native trees in protected bushland.
Now a court has fined Yi Wang $187,500 for his role in organising and carrying out the destruction of 287 trees from a council-owned foreshore bushland at Woodford Bay in Longueville in late 2023.
The New South Wales land and environment court justice Rachel Pepper convicted Wang last week for helping to orchestrate the clearing of 1,210 sq metres of land beside a waterfront property on Lucretia Avenue.
Wang pleaded guilty to three offences in relation to the unlawful clearing, which Pepper heard destroyed potential habitat for a range of protected and threatened animals, including powerful owls and microbats. It could take three decades to recover.
The unlawful tree clearing also greatly reduced the natural protection previously afforded to an Aboriginal midden, the court heard.
When it sold in 2014 for $7.6m, real estate agents described the Lucretia Avenue property as an “exclusive waterfront” residence commanding “water views from every room”. It boasted a private beach and was “bordering lush reserves”.
The director of Sydney Garden Home, Wang was hired by the stepdaughter of the owner of the adjacent property to the bushland, Yao Wu, for grass trimming work in November 2023.
The following day, Wu asked Wang to clear trees as well, including on public land.
“This is my back yard,” Wang would later claim Wu repeatedly told him.
Wang then hired casual labourers, including a chainsaw operator, and chopped down and removed trees over a 12-day period. The gardener sent regular updates on the progress of the work to his employer via WeChat and was paid in cash, which was often left in a shoe at the front of the adjacent property for Wang to collect.
Lane Cove council would later call those dozen days “the worst act of environmental vandalism” in the area’s history. The mayor, Scott Bennison, said the “outrageous” act needed to be “prosecuted to the full extent possible”.
In September 2024, the council installed a huge double-sided banner on the site of what it labelled “tree vandalism”, demonstrating its “commitment to obscure” harbour views gained by the destruction of the habitat and pledging it would remain in place until the trees grew back “to a suitable height”.
In addition to the fine and the publication of notices about the case in newspapers, Pepper ordered Wang to pay Lane Cove council’s legal costs.
In a statement, the council said it welcomed the judgment, describing it as “a win for native bushland”.
As it was awaiting the outcome of another matter before the court relating to the same location, the council declined to comment further.
The case first came to light through a tip-off from a member of the public. A council ranger then visited the site the day after the last day of clearing. Council officers discovered no approvals, permits, or consents had been issued for any tree removal and private investigators were engaged.
Recorded interviews from those investigators, as well as CCTV footage and invoices from a nearby dump, which showed Wang and the chainsaw operator disposing of ute loads of branches and vegetation, provided evidence for a timeline of events and facts that Wang did not dispute.
The council commissioned expert reports on the impact of the clearing, including by an arborist, a geologist and a senior archaeologist.
Wang argued his conduct was not reckless but rather negligent at its highest.
Pepper accepted references from his wife, mother and friend that Wang was otherwise a person of good character and was unlikely to reoffend.
The native forest canopy he helped clear had stood since at least 1943 and included an endangered ecological community.
Regeneration of the trees to a comparable ecological condition would probably take 20 to 30 years, a period during which regrowth would be susceptible to pathogens and weed invasion, the court heard.

title: ‘Very Debilitating’: Hunter Biden Says His Father’s Cancer Has Spread Further
summary: Hunter Biden shared an update on former President Joe Biden’s condition on Friday, explaining that his cancer is worsening.
full_text:
Former President Joe Biden’s cancer has spread “further,” his son Hunter Biden told the BBC on Friday.
In an interview on Newsnight, Hunter Biden described how difficult it was to see his 83-year-old father battling the disease, which was first shared with the public in May 2025.
“The cancer has spread, metastasized into his bones and further,” he said. “It’s very painful and it’s very debilitating in many respects.”
Hunter Biden did not elaborate on where else the cancer had spread, and the former President’s office has not publicly disclosed additional details about the extent of the disease.
Joe Biden had surgery to remove skin cancer lesions in September last year and completed a round of radiation therapy for prostate cancer in October.
As his wife, Jill Biden, told Kelly Ripa last week on the podcast Let’s Talk Off Camera With Kelly Ripa, their family understands that the disease will be part of his life for the rest of his life.
“He will live forever with cancer,” she told Ripa. “It’s daily. And I think it’s challenging.”
Hunter Biden also acknowledged to host Paddy O’Connell that his father’s well-being may have been affected by the strain that his struggles with addiction, and their consequences, brought.
“Maybe you shouldn't have allowed your dad to run,” O’Connell said, suggesting that these serious concerns might have been a distraction from the demands of the office.
“The idea that I allow my father to do anything, to this very day, is laughable to me,” Hunter Biden said, while insisting that he fully supports his father, knowing that he always made his decisions with their family and the American public in mind. “There is no taking the keys away from a President.”
“Where were you when your father failed to complete a sentence on prime-time television,” O’Connell said, alluding to Biden’s widely criticized debate with Donald Trump, which set the stage for him stepping down as the Democratic presidential nominee in 2024.
Hunter Biden said that he was watching and that he found the moment “shocking,” adding: “I also know that he obviously had cancer. Whether it was impacting him or not, nine months later he was diagnosed with Stage 4 prostate cancer and Stage 4 metastatic bone cancer—none of which we knew.”
According to a statement issued at the time, Joe Biden was diagnosed “with prostate cancer, with a Gleason score of 9 (Grade Group 5) with metastasis to the bone.” Despite the aggressive diagnosis, the former President’s office also said that the cancer “appears to be hormone-sensitive which allows for effective management.”
Jill Biden said in an interview with CBS’s Sunday Morning in May 2026 that the diagnosis had come as a surprise, explaining that men over 70 are not routinely screened for prostate cancer since it’s usually a “slow-growing cancer” and the harms of repeat screenings can outweigh the good. She added, "I do feel we had amazing care in the White House, but somehow that was missed."
Hunter Biden insisted that, despite leaving the Oval Office, his father’s work is not yet done.
Joe Biden remains “out there,” speaking publicly about the issues that are important to him, his son insisted.
“He’s still doing his thing,” he said. “He so believes in this country.”
That included appearing as a keynote speaker at the Maryland Democratic Party Gala in June.
“As long as he’s alive,” his son said, “I promise you, he is going to continue to fight.”
Hunter Biden’s convictions and presidential pardon
In June 2024, while his father began in earnest to pursue a second term, Hunter Biden was convicted of three felonies related to purchasing and possessing a firearm while addicted to a controlled substance. He also pleaded guilty to nine federal tax charges, including failure to pay $1.4 million from 2016 to 2019.
Weeks before leaving office and following repeated assurances on the campaign trail that he would not do so, then-President Joe Biden made the controversial choice to pardon his son for what he considered unfair and politically motivated persecution.
“From the day I took office, I said I would not interfere with the Justice Department’s decision-making, and I kept my word even as I have watched my son being selectively and unfairly prosecuted,” Biden wrote on Dec. 1, 2024, in announcing his change of heart.
He granted Hunter Biden a “full and unconditional pardon” for any criminal acts committed or alleged going back 10 years. On his final day in office, he also preemptively pardoned several family members, including his brother, James Biden, citing fear of retaliation against his family from the incoming Trump Administration.
The decision drew substantial criticism from both sides of the aisle, which Hunter Biden acknowledged to O’Connell.
“Was it good for our Constitution? Was it good for the American people? Was it good for my dad’s legacy? No, on all counts,” he said. “It’s something that is easily criticized, and for good reason, and I can’t pretend otherwise.”
However, he added that his father’s concerns about the incoming President were likely well-founded.
“I think that Donald Trump has proven to be exactly who my dad thought he was going to be, as it relates to the revenge and retribution that he would seek on his political enemies,” he said.
The Biden family’s history with cancer
The Bidens have long advocated for comprehensive cancer research. Joe Biden’s eldest son, Beau, whom he had with his first wife Neilia Hunter Biden, died of glioblastoma, a type of brain cancer, in 2015.
“Cancer uses every tool at its disposal — it hides from the immune system, builds its own blood supply, uses viruses to spread, engineers a friendly cellular environment to support its survival and growth, and knows how to spread through the body by using pathways and mutations we do not understand fully,” the 46th President and his wife, Jill, wrote in an article for TIME in 2017, sharing their reasons for launching the Biden Cancer Initiative. “Cancer never gives up; it never surrenders.”
The Biden Cancer Initiative built on Joe Biden’s commitment during his Vice Presidency to work on a “national commitment to end cancer as we know it,” which became the Cancer Moonshot Initiative, announced in a State of the Union by then-President Barack Obama in 2016.
Joe Biden will release his memoir, “Promise Me, America,” on Nov. 17.

title: BTCPay restricts remote Lightning access after attackers steal funds
summary: Foundation and Citadel21 reported drained Lightning nodes, but the total amount stolen and number of affected operators remain unknown.
full_text:
BTCPay restricts remote Lightning access after attackers steal funds
Foundation and Citadel21 reported drained Lightning nodes, but the total amount stolen and number of affected operators remain unknown.
BTCPay Server has temporarily restricted public remote connections to Lightning Network nodes running Lightning Network Daemon (LND) software after attackers exploited a critical vulnerability to obtain credentials and move funds.
BTCPay said the restriction prevents external wallets such as Zeus from connecting through a BTCPay Server domain or Tor onion address on Docker deployments. BTCPay said Lightning payments can continue and that it plans to restore the remote-access option when it considers it safe.
Version 2.4.2 installs LND version 0.21.1 and automatically regenerates the macaroon credentials on standard BTCPay installations. The project advised operators to check for unauthorized payments, unexpected channel closures, unfamiliar peers and discrepancies in their onchain or Lightning balances.
The BTCPay breach is the latest security incident involving widely used Bitcoin products, following a Coldcard hardware-wallet flaw linked to more than $100 million in confirmed losses. The separate incidents affected software surrounding Bitcoin rather than the network’s underlying protocol.
Update automatically rotates Lightning credentials
BTCPay said the vulnerability allowed an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain “macaroon” credential files used to control LND, an implementation of the Lightning Network. The project said the exposed credentials could allow attackers to take control of an LND node and move its funds.
According to the project’s security advisory, version 2.4.2 installs LND version 0.21.1 and automatically regenerates macaroon credentials on standard BTCPay installations. It advised operators to check for unauthorized payments, unexpected channel closures, unfamiliar peers and discrepancies between their records and onchain or Lightning balances.
Related: Coldcard exploit pushes July losses to $247M as second-worst month of 2026
BTCPay also said operators exposing LND through their own reverse proxy, Tor service, forwarded port, or another route outside BTCPay must rotate their credentials separately. The project said installing the update does not close access routes managed independently by the operator.
At least two operators publicly reported losses. Foundation CEO Zach Herbert said the hardware-wallet company’s Lightning node was drained overnight. He later clarified that its hot wallet was unaffected, while its Lightning channels were closed and the funds swept.
Bitcoin publication Citadel21 also reported that its Lightning node had been swept. Neither operator disclosed the amount lost.

title: 大賣空 Burry 警告 1987 崩盤重演，彭博專欄反駁：萬年空頭「錯多對少」
summary:
知名空頭 Michael Burry 再度搬出「1987 式崩盤」劇本，警告標普 500 屢創新高背後藏著系統 […]

〈大賣空 Burry 警告 1987 崩盤重演，彭博專欄反駁：萬年空頭「錯多對少」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
知名空頭 Michael Burry 再度搬出「1987 式崩盤」劇本，警告標普 500 屢創新高背後藏著系統性風險；彭博專欄作家 Jonathan Levin 撰文反駁，指出這類末日警語的命中率長期偏低。
（前情提要：大賣空 Michael Burry 再警告：美股有閃崩危險！量化基金成拋售潮來臨）
（背景補充：大賣空 Burry 警告納指本益比 43 倍「押注半導體跌 30%」：像車禍前幾分鐘、類 .com 泡沫將來臨）
美股歷史上，「1987 重演」幾乎是每次指數創新高時都會被翻出來的固定劇本。本週標普 500 指數上漲 3.37%，再次改寫歷史新高。知名的大空頭 Michael Burry 就在 8 月 4 日於其電子報中寫道：「波動率減弱迫使波動率目標基金提高槓桿，並帶動其他動能策略運用的槓桿。」
他指的是避險基金與系統性交易策略的共同特徵，波動率走低時自動加碼曝險，一旦波動率反彈又會急踩煞車、反手拋售。全球以波動率為目標調節部位的基金規模估計約達 2 兆美元。他目前仍押注 Nvidia、Tesla、Palantir 等 AI 概念股走跌，理由是 AI 基礎建設的資本支出仰賴可能難以持續的融資結構。
1987 的教訓，被引用對了嗎？
不過彭博專欄作家 Levin 認為，Burry 聚焦波動率機制的論述，確實讓人聯想到 1987 年 10 月 19 日「黑色星期一」，道瓊工業指數當天重挫 22.6%，至今仍是史上單日最大跌幅紀錄。
當年助長崩盤的機制是投資組合保險，電腦程式在股價下跌時自動加碼賣出以避險，賣壓與跌勢彼此強化，最終釀成惡性迴圈。Levin 也同意這類系統性風險確實值得監管單位提前防範，就像消防演練，一旦警報響起，所有人幾乎會在同一時間衝向逃生門。
但他話鋒一轉：把這種風險提示直接當成進出場時機的操作訊號，恐怕沒有太大用處。他指出，由市場內部動能驅動的閃崩，只要基本面沒有惡化，通常會出現急遽反彈；Burry 只強調 1987 年跌得有多重，卻沒提 1988 年幾乎立刻收復失土、1989 年更是一路刷新高點。
躲過崩盤，不代表躲得掉之後的漲勢
就算真有人在黑色星期一前夕精準出清持股，若沒辦法同樣精準抓住重返市場的時間點，這筆交易終究不划算，而抓對回補時機正是長期看空者最弱的一環，這也是 Levin 認為長期持有策略優於擇時操作的原因。
他同時指出，標普 500 目前的本益比雖已來到歷史相對高檔，企業獲利動能卻是他印象中數一數二強勁的階段；歷史經驗顯示，指數寫下空前新高後，往往會催生更多空前新高，而非立即反轉。

full_text:
Higgsfield 把 95 分鐘 AI 電影《Hell Grind》整包開源，每一句提示詞、每一份素材、每一次迭代版本全部公開，還附上 19 分鐘幕後拆解與一套打包成 Claude Skill 的提示詞工具。

（背景補充：ComfyUI 估值衝上 5 億美元：AI 影像不想靠抽卡，讓創作者掌控每一幀輸出）
熱門 AI 影片生成平台 Higgsfield，近期開源了長達 95 分鐘的 AI 電影《Hell Grind》全部提示詞、角色模型與場景素材，還附上一支十九分鐘的幕後拆解影片，把片中最大一場打鬥戲從零重建一次：提示詞怎麼改、改了幾次、哪一次失敗，全部攤開來給人看。
對想學 AI 生影片的人來說，官方如何生成這些鏡頭、團隊踩過的坑、寫壞的提示詞、以及後來怎麼修…這些經驗都非常有價值。
成本花費約 50 萬美元
《Hell Grind》是由 15 人團隊在哈薩克阿拉木圖花 14 天做出來的，總成本接近 50 萬美元，其中將近八成、約 40 萬美元砸在 GPU 雲端算力上，剩下兩成才是人事。
執行長 Alex Mashrabov 形容整個生成過程「有種吃角子老虎機的感覺」，燒錢燒到最後，253 個能用的鏡頭是從 16,181 次生成裡篩出來的，比例約 64 比 1。這次開源背後還有一層算盤，就是為 Higgsfield 自己辦的 Higgsfield Global Film Festival 宣傳，總獎金 100 萬美元、首獎 50 萬。
開源包裡裝了什麼？
官方開源專案頁裡有完整細節，每一句提示詞、每一份素材、每一次迭代版本都在，理論上任何人都能照著重建一次（願意燒錢的話）。所有角色、場景、素材被攤在同一張工作區裡，隨時在視野內，不用在資料夾裡東翻西找。
官方還打包了一支 Claude 的 Skill，按一個加號、上傳檔案，約 30 秒就能用。
這個 Skill 吐出來的提示詞是固定的四段式結構：
- 先用簡單錨點標記素材，例如 @Roco、@Monster，每個標記綁一段簡短外型描述與參考圖，模型才不用猜
- 接著把空間座標鎖到公尺
- 再把動作寫成以秒計的時間碼
- 最後加一條嚴格規則，擋掉模型自己亂編的部分。
開拍前，先把角色定裝
正式生成之前，團隊第一步是先把會反覆出場的角色與場景「定裝」。
角色的髮型、臉譜、穿著…等基礎造型；怪物設定寫死成 4 公尺高、骷髏臉、紅水晶刀刃，而且沒有右手，骨頭直接從手肘長成刀刃。細節寫得越詳細，模型每次生成越容易辨識同一個角色。
提示詞怎麼寫，才不會一路爛下去
第一條原則：相機運動別用形容詞，要用比較級與具體數字。不寫「鏡頭快一點」，要寫「比典型電影推軌快 3 倍」；環繞軌道寫成從 8 公尺拉近到 4 公尺、高度從 3 公尺降到 2 公尺；怪物變身的時間直接給硬數字 0.4 秒。
官方的說法是，影片模型不太懂「戲劇性」這種抽象詞。簡單來說就是，模型不吃形容詞，只吃數字。
群眾規模也一樣不報數字，用三層堆疊：前景一名清晰的戰士、後方密集人群、再後面淡入霧裡的剪影，實際看得清楚的大概只有 40 人，剩下的交給觀眾大腦自己補完。濃霧甚至被當成除錯手段，把能見度壓到 20 公尺，背景生成崩壞的部分就被藏起來（官方補充，現在模型的 4K 算圖背景已經穩很多，這招重要性下降，但畫面塞滿東西時仍然好用）。
動作也拆成半秒級步驟，前景武士起身被切成手部 0.5 秒、頭盔 1.5 秒、站直 3 秒，時間寫死，模型才不會搶拍或跳過中間階段。最後一條紀律最土也最有效：每次至少跑四段生成，才分得出來是隨機出包還是提示詞本身有問題。分得出壞提示詞和壞手氣，才是省算力額度的關鍵。
這場戲用的生成設定也被公開：模型固定成 CS 2.0、單段 15 秒、每次輸出四段，沒有任何隱藏設定。
最貴的一課：別叫模型「不要」
官方稱這次學到最貴的一課，不是怎麼寫，是怎麼不寫。片中怪物右手那顆鏡頭，提示詞明寫「沒有手持物、沒有刀柄」，模型照樣塞一隻手握著劍。團隊後來反過來，叫模型把手臂抬高、讓畫面清楚看到那裡什麼都沒有，才解決。
更貴的一次，是整場打戲拍出「電玩過場動畫」的感覺。團隊寫了十幾次「不是遊戲」「不要 CGI」，模型看不懂「不」，只認得句子裡一堆「遊戲」兩個字，於是照著做出遊戲感。
修法有兩步：把禁令換成正面描述，不寫「不要廉價特效」，直接說清楚要什麼樣的光線與材質；再來是改成多鏡剪接，因為一鏡到底本來就是電玩慣用的拍法，真電影會剪。團隊乾脆讓模型自己當導演切四刀，各配一組鏡位——50mm 環繞、24mm 低角度、85mm 特寫、35mm 廣角。
跨鏡銜接也得明寫死規則：第一鏡結尾的姿勢，等於第二鏡開頭的姿勢，不然 AI 會把剪接點當成全新場景，姿勢直接歸零重來。打擊感同樣寫成物理，不寫「時間變慢」，而是把兩把刀的距離逐秒標到公分，碰撞角度也寫清楚，再加一條硬規則：水晶永遠贏鋼鐵，模型就會讓鋼刀碎裂、噴出火花。
官方最後總結：這套工作流真正的技術，不是寫出一句天才提示詞，而是看懂哪裡壞了、只修那裡，片中很多鏡頭，其實是從同一批生成裡挑出兩段不同的片段剪在一起。

title: 制衡中俄》五角大廈擬授權總統彈性動用戰術核彈，反對者憂連鎖失控
summary:
五角大廈醞釀核武新戰略，授權總統更彈性動用戰術核武以嚇阻中俄，批評者憂心此舉恐降低核戰門檻。 （前情提要：法國 […]

〈制衡中俄》五角大廈擬授權總統彈性動用戰術核彈，反對者憂連鎖失控〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
五角大廈醞釀核武新戰略，授權總統更彈性動用戰術核武以嚇阻中俄，批評者憂心此舉恐降低核戰門檻。
（前情提要：法國 1990 年代以來首度擴充核武！馬克宏宣布增加核彈頭數量，美國承諾不再可靠？）
（背景補充：外媒爆料川普提出的美伊「15 點和平方案」：伊朗須全面棄核換解除制裁，中東局勢現轉機？）
2026 年 2 月 5 日，美俄之間近半世紀的「核武限武機制」正式畫下句點，從 2010 年簽署的新戰略武器裁減條約（New START）在沒有替代方案的情況下屆滿失效。這份條約原本把雙方部署在戰略載具上的核彈頭數量鎖在 1,550 枚的天花板，如今這道天花板不再具有法律約束力。
值得注意的是，這份條約管的從來只是「大」的一端：戰略核武；戰術核武完全不在規範範圍內，而這正是俄羅斯手握顯著數量優勢的領域。美軍戰略司令部今年估計，俄國目前擁有多達 2,000 枚戰術核彈頭，一枚都不受任何條約限制。
數字裡的漏洞：條約管了「大的」，放過「小的」
除了 1550 枚彈頭這個上限，New START 另外還設有兩道防線：700 枚已部署飛彈與重型轟炸機、800 具已部署與未部署的發射載具。
三道防線攤開來看，管的全都是能一次抹去一座城市等級的武力；但對彈頭當量較小、專打軍事編隊與基地的戰術核武，條約從頭到尾沒有著墨一個字。
這種「管大放小」的軍控設計，原本建立在戰術核武毀滅性有限、不至於失控的假設上，但當俄羅斯手握 2000 枚不受監管的戰術彈頭，而華府卻只能靠戰略核武嚇阻時，這個假設本身就出現裂縫。
批評者形容，這種一方受限、一方不受限的狀態，對美國構成「無法容忍的劣勢」，五角大廈現在要補的，正是當初條約留下的這一塊空白。
柯伯吉密赴戰略司令部，選址本身就是一種表態
2026 年 8 月，五角大廈就啟動了一項聚焦戰術核武的戰略檢討。
主導這項戰略檢討的，是現任戰爭部政策次長 Elbridge Colby。根據 NBC News 引述 5 名知情人士的獨家報導，他將在造訪內布拉斯加州美軍戰略司令部期間，於一場非公開軍事活動中說明計畫細節。
選在戰略司令部，全美唯一統籌核武戰力的作戰司令部，而非透過白宮記者會或國防部公開簡報對外說明，某種程度上透露這項計畫的成熟度已經不低；選擇這個場合，更像是在為後續實際執行鋪路，而非單純放話測風向。
戰術核武是什麼？從區域打擊到總統決策空間
報導指出，這項檢討的核心，是把戰術核武的地位拉高到不遜於遠端戰略打擊力量。
所謂戰術核武，通常鎖定戰區或區域層級的軍事目標，例如軍事編隊、基地或特定設施，而非以摧毀整座城市、瓦解對手全部核武力量為目的；搭配的載具射程也相對較短，設計邏輯更接近點狀打擊而非全面清除。
報導也提到，新戰略設想的情境是：一旦北京或莫斯科對美國盟國動手，華府必須能在不立即升級為全面核戰的前提下做出對應回應。這也反映出美軍近年愈發正視一項處境，過去數十年美國面對的核對手多半只有一個，如今卻要同時盤算中國、俄羅斯兩條戰線各自的核武動向，這在冷戰結束後的美軍規劃史上並不常見。
川普手上的選項空間被開啟
支援這項轉變的官員主張，白宮在全面核戰之外理應多出幾道可執行的回應層次，讓對手評估局勢時知道華府手上不是只有「按或不按」兩種選擇，藉此墊高嚇阻的說服力。
一名五角大廈高層向 NBC News 說明時強調，華府需要的是真正拿得出手、對手會相信的核選項，而不是只存在於檔案上的威懾。五角大廈對這項政策目標的表述是：用實際且可信的選項擴大總統的決策空間，藉此強化嚇阻。
換句話說，這項檢討實質上是在為總統川普，以及未來歷任總統，開啟更寬的決策空間，讓動用戰術核武不再是全有或全無的單一選擇。
但這套說法立刻招來質疑。批評者警告，一旦動用戰術核武的心理關卡被拉低，武力選項與外交折衝之間原本該有的緩衝地帶就會被壓縮，原本得經過層層升級才輪得到的戰術核武，如今可能因為一次區域摩擦就提早被擺上選項清單，讓原本還留有轉圜餘地的區域性衝突，更容易一步步滑向失控。
靠默契維持上限，沒有法律約束力的脆弱現狀
據 Axios 今年 2 月報導，美俄雙方一度就條約失效後仍非正式遵守 New START 限額接近達成共識，但最終沒有取得任何具法律約束力的結果。
這意味著自 2026 年 2 月 5 日以來，雙方戰略核武數量之所以還大致維持在條約原本設下的水位，靠的不是查核機制，而是彼此默契與剋制；一旦任何一方認為局勢需要，隨時可以片面突破而不違反任何條約，因為條約已經不存在了。戰術核武的鬆綁若在這個時間點上路，等於在軍控真空之外再疊加一層決策彈性的鬆動。
批評者也提醒，武器分類上的「戰術」字眼，跟實際殺傷力是兩回事，核爆造成的慘重傷亡、放射性落塵擴散與連鎖報復，不會因為彈頭當量較小或射程較短而消失。接下來幾個觀察重點包括：白宮最終會把這項檢討採納到什麼程度、俄羅斯與中國是否會以擴充戰術核武部署作為回應，以及這是否會催化新一輪不受條約規範的軍備競賽。

title: 加密 U 卡單月消費破 7.5 億美元、880 萬筆交易：穩定幣刷進日常消費
summary:
a16z 最新數據顯示，加密支付卡 7 月刷卡金額達 7.59 億美元、880 萬筆交易，年增數倍；USDC […]

〈加密 U 卡單月消費破 7.5 億美元、880 萬筆交易：穩定幣刷進日常消費〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
a16z 最新數據顯示，加密支付卡 7 月刷卡金額達 7.59 億美元、880 萬筆交易，年增數倍；USDC 已取代歐元穩定幣成為主流計價單位。
（前情提要：加密U卡「月消費達 6 億美元」年增 6 倍！USDT 佔 62.5%、Visa 吃下 9 成，Jupiter 單月翻 6.6 倍）
（背景補充：香港穩定幣獨角獸 RedotPay 衝刺赴美 IPO，但彭博揭高管頻繁流失、中國關聯隱患）
穩定幣正在被大量「刷卡」使用於日常消費。根據 a16z crypto 今日在 X 公布的最新資料，加密支付卡在 7 月的月刷卡金額達到 7.59 億美元，較一年前的 3.06 億美元成長超過 2.5 倍；同月交易筆數逼近 880 萬筆，也比去年同期的 520 萬筆成長近 7 成。
加密支付卡讓用戶能在任何接受傳統卡片網路的地方以加密資產消費；背後的運作邏輯是，持卡人手上的加密資產（大多數是穩定幣），會在結帳當下被自動換成當地法幣，因此在商家端看起來就跟一般刷卡毫無差異。
Growth in the number of purchases made with crypto payment cards is trending similarly to the growth in crypto card volume. Nearly 9 million purchases were made using crypto payment cards during July, up from about 5.2 million a year ago.
That puts the average amount spent per… https://t.co/wMhgjooVKV pic.twitter.com/Qg4v9M8wQJ
— a16z crypto (@a16zcrypto) August 8, 2026
目前市場上有多家發卡方案並行，包括 RedotPay、EtherFi、KAST、Karta、Plasma One、Tria、Wirex One 等，其中 RedotPay 的刷卡金額規模最大，是整體成長曲線裡貢獻最多的一塊。
880 萬筆交易背後：平均客單價 86 美元
金額成長的同時，交易筆數也在同步放大。a16z crypto 指出，7 月的加密卡交易筆數約 880 萬筆，一年前僅約 520 萬筆，換算下來平均每筆消費金額落在 86 美元左右，大致落在一般日常消費（餐飲、購物、訂閱服務）的區間，而不是單筆大額轉帳。
這也點出加密卡的定位跟過去的鏈上轉帳完全不同：持卡人不需要開立傳統銀行帳戶，依方案設計，可以把穩定幣存入發卡機構代為保管，也可以直接以自我保管的方式持有在鏈上，出示卡片消費時再即時兌換。
對穩定幣持有者而言，這是把鏈上資產轉換成日常消費力最直接的一條路徑；對全球許多地區的用戶而言，這張卡也等於間接取得一個美元帳戶。
穩定幣版圖大風吹
支撐這波成長的幣種結構，也在過去兩年出現戲劇性翻轉。
根據 Paymentscan 的資料，2026 年 7 月的加密卡消費中，USDC 佔比達 58%、USDT 佔 26%，兩者合計超過 8 成；但把時間拉回 2024 年初，當時歐元穩定幣 EURe 一度囊括高達 88% 的份額。短短兩年間，主流穩定幣的江山就從歐元系穩定幣易主給以美元計價的 USDC 與 USDT，某種程度上也反映出加密卡的使用場景正從歐洲市場擴大到更廣的全球範圍。
自行申報資料與集中度風險
不過，這組資料並非沒有疑慮。撐起最大份額的 RedotPay，其刷卡數字屬於發卡方自行申報，並非全數可在鏈上驗證，Paymentscan 的資料庫本身也坦言，涵蓋範圍同時包含「可歸因至受追蹤發卡方案的鏈上活動」與「部分方案由發卡方自行回報的鏈下消費」兩種來源，準確度取決於發卡機構申報的誠實度。
成長也高度集中在少數幾個方案身上：金額端由 RedotPay 領跑，筆數端則是 RedotPay、EtherFi、Bitget Wallet 等少數幾家瓜分絕大部分市佔，一旦其中任一家的申報口徑或營運狀況出現變化，都可能讓整體曲線大幅擺動。
更別提，7.59 億美元放進全球傳統卡片支付市場動輒數兆美元的規模裡，目前仍然只是零頭；各地監管機構對加密卡發卡機構的 KYC、外匯管制與消費者保護規範也仍在持續補洞中，都是這條成長曲線能否延續的變數。
即便如此，加密卡真正的意義，在於它替沒有健全銀行體系的地區，開出一條取得美元帳戶的旁路。對穩定幣持有者來說，這張卡把原本只能在鏈上流轉的資產，變成走進超商、餐廳就能刷出去的日常消費力，這才是穩定幣「大規模應用」最貼近生活的一種樣貌。

title: 波克夏終結連 14 季賣股！淨買入 200 億美元股票，阿貝爾加碼 Alphabet 擠進五大持股
summary:
波克夏 2026 年第二季稅後淨利年增逾 1 倍至 256.67 億美元，同時連續 14 季淨賣出股票的紀錄畫 […]

〈波克夏終結連 14 季賣股！淨買入 200 億美元股票，阿貝爾加碼 Alphabet 擠進五大持股〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
波克夏 2026 年第二季稅後淨利年增逾 1 倍至 256.67 億美元，同時連續 14 季淨賣出股票的紀錄畫下句點，在新執行長阿貝爾主導下轉為淨買方，同時祭出五年來最大手筆的庫藏股回購。
（前情提要：巴菲特認錯：沒早買 Google 是大錯！至今「更有可能成為贏家」）
（背景補充：波克夏現金儲備 3817 億美元再創新高，巴菲特連續 12 季淨賣出股票「保持審慎」）
波克夏過去 14 季的操作慣性，終於在這一季被打破。阿貝爾主導的資本配置團隊在 2026 年第二季財報中，交出淨買進約 200 億美元股票的成績單，結束連續 14 個季度淨賣出的紀錄，寫下三年來首度轉為淨買方的一頁。
當中最受矚目的一筆，是斥資約 100 億美元建立的 Alphabet (GOOGL-US) ，直接擠進波克夏五大持股，取代原本的雪佛龍 (CVX-US)。
Alphabet 建倉背後的路徑差異
值得玩味的是，阿貝爾稍早才主導協助 Alphabet 敲定 850 億美元的融資案，緊接著波克夏就出手建倉。
這種「先做成生意、再買進股票」的路徑，跟巴菲特過去慣用「先看財報、再決定持股」的選股邏輯明顯不同，某種程度反映出阿貝爾看科技巨頭的角度更接近產業內部人，而不是單純的財務分析師思維。
這種操作邏輯其實也呼應波克夏過去在能源、鐵路等重資產產業慣用的「先掌握營運細節、再決定資金部位」打法，只是這回套用到科技股上，格外少見。
保險降溫、獲利結構向投資傾斜
與加碼科技股的積極形成對比，保險這塊反而降溫：第二季保險承保利潤降至 17.31 億美元，保險投資收益也年減近 10%，是財報中少見的降溫訊號。
保險承保利潤下滑與投資收益暴增同時發生，凸顯波克夏的獲利結構正從過去靠承保賺錢，逐漸往靠投資賺錢傾斜，這種轉變雖然短期墊高淨利數字，但也代表獲利波動度會被市場行情放大，不再像過去那樣穩定可預期。
另外這裡還藏著一個容易被忽略的訊號：承保利潤是靠核保紀律與風險定價堆出來的，本質上是一種可持續的經營能力；投資利得則是股票市場當下報價的產物，跟波克夏做了什麼幾乎無關。
兩者在會計上都算進淨利，但含金量卻天差地遠。當淨利愈來愈依賴股價的浮動，單季財報數字的參考價值就會被稀釋，真正該盯的是營業利潤這條線，而不是淨利本身。這也是為什麼巴菲特退休前一再提醒外界，別拿單季淨利去評價波克夏。
波克夏第二季稅後淨利來到 256.67 億美元，相較去年同期的 123.70 億美元幾乎翻倍成長；上半年累計淨利則衝上 357.73 億美元，年增幅度約 111%。撐起這波跳升的關鍵是投資收益，第二季稅後投資收益入帳 126.84 億美元，其中 109 億美元來自未實現利得，另外 18 億美元屬已實現利得。
現金水位鬆動，庫藏股買最兇的一季
資金動用的痕跡也反映在現金儲備上。截至 6 月 30 日，波克夏帳上現金降至 3,655 億美元，較上一季高點約 3,817 億美元縮水逾 160 億美元，主要動因是股票加碼與兩筆實體收購同時吃緊資金，緊接著登場的庫藏股回購更進一步收緊水位。
即便如此，這個水位仍遠高於多數同業，護城河沒有真正被撼動，只是「現金為王」的保守姿態，確實比過去幾季鬆動了一些。
接續現金水位的變化，庫藏股操作是另一個吃錢大戶。第二季買回金額衝上 45.27 億美元，寫下五年來單季新高，對比第一季僅 2.35 億美元的規模，落差相當懸殊。
光是 6 月單月，波克夏累計買進逾 714 萬股 B 股（均價約 487.98 美元），另外加碼 413 股 A 股（均價約 73.38 萬美元）。阿貝爾對外給出的理由很直接：公司內在價值已經高於市價，重啟庫藏股是理所當然的選擇。上半年庫藏股支出合計約 47.6 億美元。
本業獲利分布：誰在衝、誰在放緩
能源部門與製造服務暨零售是本業獲利的兩根支柱，BNSF 則明顯放緩。
第二季營業利潤 129.83 億美元，年增守在 16% 上下；拉長到上半年來看，累計數字來到 243.29 億美元，增速略升至約 17%。
細看板塊，能源部門增速最快，達 27%，對應 8.91 億美元；製造服務暨零售增速 24%，貢獻金額最大，共 44.70 億美元；BNSF 只交出個位數的 6% 成長，金額 15.58 億美元。
匯兌由虧轉盈，幫「其他」專案額外貢獻 12.74 億美元，屬於匯率紅利，不宜當作常態獲利看待。
三線同開的資本配置
除了股票與庫藏股，實體收購同樣動作不斷。今年 1 月，波克夏砸下約 94 億美元收購西方石油旗下化工事業 OxyChem，第二季已替營收添了約 14 億美元進帳；7 月下旬再以每股 72.5 美元、總價約 68 億美元現金買下住宅建商 Taylor Morrison。兩筆收購合計動用資金約 162 億美元，規模不算小。
分析近期操盤風格，巴菲特晚年的按兵不動常被解讀為對估值的紀律堅持，但代價是整輪科技股行情幾乎與波克夏無緣，他後來也親口承認，當初沒有及早重壓 Google 是判斷失誤。
阿貝爾接手之後，路線明顯不同：在利率高檔、房市轉冷的環境下，同時對科技股與住宅建商加碼，等於是押注利率終將回落、庫存終將去化。這個賭注不是沒有風險，如果高利率停留的時間比市場預期更久，這類實體資產收購的回本期只會被拉得更長。但對長期股東而言，資金願意重新動起來，本身就是最值得留意的訊號。
細看數字，上半年波克夏先賣出股票 277.80 億美元，同時買進 394.05 億美元，兩相抵銷後淨買超 116.25 億美元，方向與去年同期淨賣出約 45 億美元完全相反。
持股名單中，Alphabet 是唯一的新面孔，其餘蘋果、美國運通、美國銀行與可口可樂則延續原有排序；五檔合計佔股票組合比重達 66%。截至 6 月底，波克夏權益投資公允價值攀升至 3237.79 億美元，帳面浮盈同步墊高到 2172.58 億美元，較年初的水位多出 260 億美元。
加上前面提到的庫藏股與兩筆實體收購，波克夏這一季等於在股票市場、庫藏股與實體併購三條線同時出手。

title: 伊朗拋六大條件：美國撤軍、賠款、解凍資產，全接受才重開荷姆茲海峽
summary:
伊朗最高國家安全委員會週六開出六大要求，要求美國永久撤軍、賠償戰爭損失並解除凍結資產，才願重新開放荷姆茲海峽； […]

〈伊朗拋六大條件：美國撤軍、賠款、解凍資產，全接受才重開荷姆茲海峽〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
伊朗最高國家安全委員會週六開出六大要求，要求美國永久撤軍、賠償戰爭損失並解除凍結資產，才願重新開放荷姆茲海峽；阿聯同日指控伊朗飛彈攻擊商船，60 天談判大限剩不到一週。
（前情提要：伊朗更新「美伊諒解備忘錄（MOU）」框架：索要 120 億鎂凍結資金、收荷姆茲海峽過路費..）
（背景補充：荷莫茲海峽重啟「有條件」！伊朗祭三大嚴苛限制：指定專屬航道、強制收過路費、受 IRGC 監督）
伊朗最高國家安全委員會週六表示，荷姆茲海峽在美國「修正其行為」之前不會重新開放，同時開出一份可能撼動海峽管理協議談判的長串要求清單。委員會秘書 Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr 在伊朗國家廣播公司刊出的聲明中列出六大條件：美國永遠不得再威脅伊朗、永久終結對伊朗及其區域盟友的戰爭、解除對伊朗港口的海上封鎖並自該區域撤軍、「完全賠償」伊朗的戰爭損失、解除制裁，以及「無條件」釋放遭凍結的資產。
60 天大限剩一週多，阿曼從中斡旋
依 6 月簽署的臨時協議，解除制裁的時程與賠償方案原本要納入最終協議，凍結資產議題則留待後續談判處理。談判最終協議的 60 天期限將在一週多後到期，雖有延長的可能，但時間壓力明顯升高。
伊朗方面透露，已接近與阿曼就海峽管理達成另一項協議，荷姆茲海峽正位於伊朗與阿曼之間。伊朗外交部長 Abbas Araghchi 週六稍早表示，雙方接近就通航達成協議，「特別是過境航道的劃定」，但他隨後在社群發文中強調，海峽重啟仍取決於其他條件，並將現況歸咎於他所稱美國違反臨時協議的行為。
身為調解方的阿曼則在週六聲明中說，討論在「正面且具建設性的氛圍」中進行，同時譴責針對海峽船隻的攻擊。
船運量腰斬，油價止跌回升
OilPrice 統計顯示，本週一到週四僅 33 艘船通過荷姆茲海峽，較前一週的 50 艘明顯萎縮，其中僅 6 艘原油油輪獲准出港。8 月 6 日伊朗公布一份限制性的海峽通行草案，禁止美國、以色列船隻通行，其餘曾傷害伊朗的國家則須先完成賠償才能通行，當天油價隨即跳漲。
布蘭特原油目前報 83.55 美元，單日上漲 1.29%；西德州中質原油（WTI）報 78.18 美元，上漲 1.15%。本週稍早市場一度因「海峽可能重啟」的樂觀情緒，讓油價跌破 80 美元關卡，如今這波漲勢已回吐了當時的樂觀氣氛。
阿聯控伊朗飛彈攻擊商船，一邊談判一邊開火
矛盾的是，伊朗一邊與阿曼商談通航細節，一邊仍持續對海峽船隻動武。
阿聯官方表示，阿布達比國營石油天然氣公司 ADNOC 旗下一艘船週六稍早在通過荷姆茲海峽時遇襲；阿聯外交部指出，攻擊船隻的飛彈由伊朗發射，屬於針對商船攻擊行動的一環。
ADNOC 聲明強調這起事故無人傷亡，但同時透露，自 2 月美國與以色列對伊朗開戰以來，已有十多艘 ADNOC 船隻在通過海峽時遭飛彈與無人機攻擊，累計 1 名船員死亡、20 人受傷。ADNOC 並未說明本次攻擊的確切位置或損害程度。
英國海事貿易作業辦公室（UKMTO）稍後補充，阿曼 Khasab 鎮以東海域有一艘船遭投射物擊中並起火，火勢已撲滅，船隻與船員均安全；UKMTO 未能確認這是否與 ADNOC 事故為同一起事件。美國政府對伊朗開出的六大要求，截至目前尚未做出回應；美方立場一貫是先就海峽通航達成可接受的協議，再解除對伊朗的封鎖行動。

title: Saudi Arabia says fire extinguished at Aramco facility in Jizan
summary: No casualties were reported after the flames broke out early on Sunday, the Saudi Energy Ministry says.
full_text:
Saudi Arabia says fire extinguished at Aramco facility in Jizan
No casualties were reported after the flames broke out early on Sunday, the Saudi Energy Ministry says.
A fire reported at a facility belonging to Saudi Arabian state oil giant Aramco has been extinguished, authorities say.
The blaze broke out early on Sunday at a site in the coastal city of Jizan, the Saudi Ministry of Energy wrote in a statement on X. No casualties were reported.

list of 4 items

- list 2 of 4Why are oil companies posting record profits amid Iran war disruption?
- list 3 of 4Why is Saudi Arabia forming a coalition to protect the Red Sea?
- list 4 of 4New front in US-Iran war escalates as Houthis fire at Saudi oil facilities
“The competent authorities are completing the necessary procedures to deal with the incident,” the ministry added.
It did not say what caused the fire.
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi armed group claimed it carried out an attack on the facility, located on the Red Sea near its border, the latest in a series of Houthi claims of strikes targeting Saudi oil sites.
A military spokesman for the Houthi led government in the capital Sanaa, Yahya Saree, wrote on X the group “succeeded in targeting the Aramco refinery in Jizan with a drone, and the strike was precise”.
He said the attack came in response to Saudi Arabia’s “breach of the airspace of the provinces of Saada and Hajjah” with drones.
There was no immediate comment on the claim from Riyadh. Al Jazeera has contacted the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The Houthis last month claimed attacks on Aramco facilities in Jizan. The Houthis also said they targeted oil installations in Yanbu, Saudi Arabia’s principal west coast export gateway.
Aramco chief Amin Nasser said last week that recent attacks on the company’s facilities had caused some production interruptions but that he was confident operations could be restored quickly. He said the attacks had no material operational or financial impact.
The attacks have added to growing strains on a 2022 truce in the war between the Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis, which took control of the capital, Sanaa, in 2014, also declared a blockade on Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea last month, threatening shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb strait.
Saudi authorities have also blamed Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq for attacks on its oil facilities.
On Friday, Riyadh signed a defence pact with Turkiye and Pakistan amid rising regional tensions from the US-Israel war on Iran.

title: World number one Sabalenka upset by Alexandrova at Canadian Open
summary: Ekaterina Alexandrov took down four-time Grand Slam singles champion Aryna Sabalenka in a three-set marathon in Toronto.
full_text:
World number one Sabalenka upset by Alexandrova at Canadian Open
Ekaterina Alexandrov took down four-time Grand Slam singles champion Aryna Sabalenka in a three-set marathon in Toronto.
World number one Aryna Sabalenka suffered a setback in her US Open build-up after she was beaten 7-6(3), 4-6, 6-4 by Russia’s Ekaterina Alexandrova in the fourth round of the Canadian Open in Toronto on Saturday.
The 16th-seeded Alexandrova fought a hard battle, lasting nearly two and a half hours, to secure her quarterfinal berth.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Arsenal complete signing of Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes
- list 2 of 4Top 10 players to watch in the 2026-27 European football season
- list 3 of 4Lionel Messi returns to Argentina after father Jorge’s death
- list 4 of 4FIFA President Gianni Infantino denies claims UEFA paid off alleged lover
Sabalenka, a four-time Grand Slam champion and reigning US Open winner, recovered from a set down to force a decider but was unable to halt Alexandrova’s aggressive shot-making in the final set.
The Belarusian broke early in the opening set before Alexandrova rallied to force a tiebreak, which the Russian won to move ahead.
Sabalenka responded by seizing control of the second set with a break for a 4-3 lead before serving out to level the match.
Alexandrova held her nerve in the decider as Sabalenka’s error count rose. Serving to stay in the match at 4-5, the top seed saved two match points, but a double fault on the third handed victory to the Russian.
“I just tried to play every single point as if it was the last one because with her, you don’t [get] a lot of chances during the match,” Alexandrova said in her on-court interview.
“Honestly, I was trying not to think about the score or anything. Just hit the ball, and that’s it.
“I’m super happy that I could win because after the second set, I thought (the chance) was already past me.”
Alexandrova will face Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina, who defeated American eighth seed Amanda Anisimova 6-2, 6-4 for a place in the semifinals.

title: Israel announces tender for 627 settler units in occupied West Bank
summary: New settlement tender in West Bank deepens Israeli efforts to sever Palestinian ties to Jerusalem, officials warn.
full_text:
Israel announces tender for 627 settler units in occupied West Bank
New illegal settlement tender in West Bank deepens Israeli efforts to sever Palestinian ties to Jerusalem, officials warn.
Israeli authorities have issued a tender for 627 new housing units in the Kochav Yaakov settlement in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission (CRRC).
The Israel Land Authority on Thursday published the tender for the project, which will be built on land in the Ramallah and al-Bireh governorate, the commission said on Saturday.

Israel set November 30 as the deadline for construction companies to submit bids, moving the project from planning to construction just 15 months after it was first approved, it said.
CRRC slammed the expansion, saying it is designed to “deepen the separation between Jerusalem and its Palestinian surroundings”.
The illegal Israeli settlement of Kochav Yaakov sits between northern Jerusalem and the twin cities of Ramallah and el-Bireh, within a cluster of settlements Israel administers under the name “Binyamin”.
According to CRRC, the new project covers 253.7 dunams (25.37 hectares or about 63 acres) and was approved by Israeli authorities on April 27, 2025.
It says the tender marks the transition from planning to the “marketing and implementation” stage of settlement construction, with the new units expected to expand the illegal settlement’s built-up area and strengthen its links to nearby settlements and access roads. It added that the decision reflects growing investment in settlements’ economic infrastructure, not just housing.
The Israeli decision is one of several the commission has tracked this year aimed at tightening Israel’s illegal control and pressure on the Palestinian region.
According to CRRC, Israeli authorities have made 12 illegal settlement tenders in the first half of 2026, including 1,138 housing units concentrated in five main settlements, alongside a separate wave of tenders for industrial zones, offices, nursing homes and tourism facilities.
Illegal settlement expansion and settler violence have surged dramatically across the occupied West Bank this year. Palestinian monitors have recorded more than 11,000 attacks by Israeli forces and settlers across the West Bank since January 2026.
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has repeatedly said Israeli settlements have “no legal validity” and constitute a “flagrant violation” of international law.
A 2024 International Court of Justice advisory opinion deemed Israel’s continued occupation of Palestinian territory unlawful.

How China’s ‘magic’ rice seeds are transforming the fortunes of Nigerian farmers
Beijing’s hands-off approach challenges traditional Western aid models, prompting Washington to counter with agribusiness interventions
Just outside the Nigerian capital Abuja, where Green Agriculture West Africa Limited (Gawal) is based, locals do not refer to the company by name, instead as the place where the Chinese supply “magic” rice seeds.
Ahmed Yusuf, 42, credits the seeds with turning around his rice business for good. Before Gawal, Yusuf’s yields averaged just 2 tonnes per hectare, putting him on the verge of forsaking farming after more than a decade of toiling.
“Each year I was making losses, and I couldn’t meet the needs of my family, so I thought, ‘what was the point?’” he recalled.
Yusuf’s fortunes changed after he was introduced to Gawal’s R1 rice strain.
“With this new variety I have been able to stay in business by increasing my yield more than threefold on basically the same effort,” he said.
Yusuf’s success is part of a broader China-backed push to transform African subsistence farming into a highly productive mechanised powerhouse. But this agricultural diplomacy is about more than food security.

title: Costa Rican diplomat emerges as strong contender to be first female head of UN
summary:
Rebeca Grynspan seen as continuity candidate with tacit support from current secretary general, António Guterres

A Costa Rican diplomat and former vice-president whose parents were refugees from the Holocaust has become the surprise frontrunner to lead the United Nations as its first female secretary general.

Rebeca Grynspan, whose parents emigrated to Central America from Poland – and whose maternal grandparents were killed by the Nazis – is the current head of the UN conference on trade and development (UNCTAD), a body that has exhaustively tallied the economic damage inflicted by Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories.

Continue reading...
full_text:
A Costa Rican diplomat and former vice-president whose parents were refugees from the Holocaust has become the surprise frontrunner to lead the United Nations as its first female secretary general.
Rebeca Grynspan, whose parents emigrated to Central America from Poland – and whose maternal grandparents were killed by the Nazis – is the current head of the UN conference on trade and development (UNCTAD), a body that has exhaustively tallied the economic damage inflicted by Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories.
The current secretary general, António Guterres, will complete his second term on 31 December 2026 and under an informal system of regional rotation his successor is expected to come from Latin America.
In a secret first straw poll of the UN security council, the five permanent and 10 temporary members were asked to say whether they supported, objected to or were neutral about each of seven candidates.
Grynspan secured 10 “encourage” votes, four “no opinion” votes and one “discourage” vote. The identity of the discourage vote is not known, but the fact that she had only one objection places her in a strong opening position. The process is likely to conclude in October.
Grynspan’s closest rival is Carolyn Rodrigues-Burkett, Guyana’s former UN envoy, with nine encourages, two discourages and four no opinions. At the close of a Bloomberg-sponsored debate at the general assembly last month she secured 49% of the vote among those attending, with Grynspan second on 14%.
“Grynspan is seen by some as the continuity candidate, having the tacit support from Guterres,” said one western diplomat. “But the key is the source of the candidate’s discouragement votes: if [the votes] are coming from Russia, China or the US, there is a risk of deadlock.”
The election comes at a critical moment for the legitimacy of multilateralism, as the UN suffers 20% job cuts and the secretary general’s role as mediator is supplanted by other actors, leaving the world body as a largely ignored moral conscience, or as a venue in which all sides vent their well-rehearsed differences.
If elected, Grynspan would be the UN’s first Jewish secretary general. The UN has been criticised for overly focusing on Israel in its debates, but Grynspan has invoked her Jewish heritage to argue for the importance of ending conflict.
She told the UN general assembly: “Peace is what made it possible for my parents, two refugees from the second world war, to find respect and dignity in a small country, Costa Rica. I am the daughter of this peace, a demonstration of what peace makes possible.”
Her sister moved to Israel as a 17-year-old to study chemistry at the Hebrew University. As a result, her niece and nephew have completed compulsory service in the Israel Defense Forces.
Under her leadership, however, UNCTAD has factually and starkly documented the economic damage wrought by Israel’s long-term occupation of the Palestinian territories.
Its landmark February 2026 report found that “cumulatively, the Palestinian economy lost an estimated $212.2bn (in constant 2015 dollars) from 2000 to 2024. This partial, estimated lost potential, equivalent to nearly 20 times the entire Palestinian GDP of 2024, stems directly from Israeli occupation policies, restrictions, closures, and recurrent military operations.”
In November 2025 Grynspan pointed out that Gaza’s GDP per capita had plummeted to $161 per person per year, one of the most severe economic contractions in modern history.
Three other candidates, including Michelle Bachelet, have probably met with too much influential opposition to secure the job. Bachelet, the former president of Chile and a former UN human rights commissioner, faces opposition from the US government, which claims she was soft on China’s human rights record. But the Trump administration’s recent suggestion that the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, should get the job symbolises America’s drift away from the UN mainstream.
The secretary general is elected to serve an initial four-year term after the 193-strong general assembly is requested to endorse a single recommendation by the security council. A candidate needs nine positive votes and no veto by a security council member.
The new candidate must be elected by the end of the year, and there will be further meetings of the security council to test opinion.

title: Russian family denied asylum in Finland fear reprisals for pro-Ukraine activism
summary:
Nikita and Olga Belov say they will be persecuted on return to Moscow but are yet to convince Finnish authorities

A Russian family faces deportation from Finland after repeatedly being denied asylum – despite the threat of arrest, imprisonment and potential torture for their pro-Ukrainian activism.

Nikita and Olga Belov fled their homeland in 2022 after attracting the attention of Russian authorities – including military summons, threatening messages and attempts to locate them – after expressing opposition to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Continue reading...
full_text:
A Russian family faces deportation from Finland after repeatedly being denied asylum – despite the threat of arrest, imprisonment and potential torture for their pro-Ukrainian activism.
Nikita and Olga Belov fled their homeland in 2022 after attracting the attention of Russian authorities – including military summons, threatening messages and attempts to locate them – after expressing opposition to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Nikita, 25, left his engineering job at a research institute in Moscow specialising in metallurgical technologies after finding out the work he was doing was connected to the Russian war effort.
Since arriving in Finland on visas, Nikita and his mother, Olga, 55, a nurse anaesthetist, have been vocal supporters of Ukraine and public in their active support and coordination of aid sent to the country and its armed forces. But the Finnish immigration service told the mother and son that despite this they face “no real risk” if they return to Russia.
In April, they were detained by Finnish authorities pending deportation. They were later released after a court intervention but are now awaiting a decision that could result in them being deported within weeks.
The Belov case is understood to be one of many of Russians being denied asylum in neighbouring Finland where legal experts deem their future risk and human rights have not been sufficiently assessed.
Between February 2022 and June 2026, the Finnish immigration service deported 1,039 Russians according to official statistics: the most of any nationality. During the same period, 1,109 of 1,342 Russians were refused entry to Finland in connection with a negative asylum application.
Since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Finland’s relationship with its neighbour has shifted drastically. Previously, Finland was a popular tourism destination for Russians and there were several well-used border crossings. It has since indefinitely closed its entire border, accusing Moscow of directing asylum seekers to Finland in a “hybrid operation”.
Russia has also expanded its military bases on the border, while Nato – which Finland joined in 2023 – has conducted training exercises in the country.
Nikita said his problems in Russia started when he realised that his boss had lied when he had told him that the project he was working on was not linked to the war effort. When he tried to come off the project, he said his boss threatened him with arrest or being sent to the frontline.
“After that I realised I cannot leave this job without consequences and that we had to think about the situation,” Nikita said. His mother, he said, was then called by the military to ask about him and their house was visited by police. They soon came to the conclusion that they had no option but to leave Russia. “Now we realise if we come back we will be arrested immediately and go to jail and be tortured,” Nikita said.
In Finland they have volunteered at their local Ukraine centre and contributed to humanitarian support, including help for first aid, food, clothes, Starlink equipment and a 3D printer, for which they received a video thank you message from Ukrainian soldiers.
“We try to adapt, try to support Ukraine, try to state our opinion, because it is very important to help Ukraine. Help them strike back,” he said.
The mother and son first applied for asylum in Finland in 2022 but it was refused, after which they unsuccessfully appealed. This year they applied again and were refused and were sent a deportation order. They were then placed in a detention centre awaiting deportation but after a court intervention were allowed to go home before a final decision. “There were all bad things in our minds. It was like the start of torture because it was a totally traumatic experience,” Nikita said. “At the time we really tried to prepare for our death.”
Since then they have suffered with their mental health and undergone panic attacks as they wait for the decision of the court.
Their lawyer, who requested not to be named for security reasons, said the Belovs are very likely to be at risk if they are deported to Russia. Nikita’s work history will also put them at risk, the lawyer said. In a previous role he said he had access to confidential government information.
While it has long been difficult to get asylum in Finland, the lawyer said that recent changes on the border and to asylum procedure, including reduced access to legal aid, has made it even harder. “It’s even more difficult to get refugee status, even with clear political opinion showing. We really have to fight these cases to get the status that was earlier easier to get.”
The political activist and Putin critic Bill Browder, who is the head of the Global Magnitsky Justice Campaign, said the case is “a defining test of Europe’s commitment to protecting those who have risked everything to oppose Putin’s war”.
Browder, whose friend and lawyer Sergei Magnitsky died at the hands of Putin’s regime, added: “If people who refused to support aggression, openly opposed the regime, and now face persecution are denied protection, it could create a dangerous precedent that discourages others from taking a stand against authoritarianism.”
A Finnish immigration service spokesperson said it could not comment on individual cases.
Antti Lehtinen, the director of the department for international protection, which is part of the Finnish immigration service, added: “The situation of each applicant is assessed individually, taking into account their personal circumstances.
“For example, opposition to the war in Ukraine and related activities may constitute grounds for persecution based on political opinion. If we assess that a person’s political opinion or activities place them at risk of persecution or serious harm in Russia, they will be granted international protection.”

title: Brazil targets crypto fraud with up to 24-hour transfer hold
summary: The rules, effective Jan. 1, 2027, cover transactions above $10,000 sent to overseas providers or self-custody wallets, along with other transfers flagged for review.
full_text:
Brazil targets crypto fraud with up to 24-hour transfer hold
The rules, effective Jan. 1, 2027, cover transactions above $10,000 sent to overseas providers or self-custody wallets, along with other transfers flagged for review.
Brazil’s central bank will require virtual asset service providers (VASPs) to place precautionary holds of up to 24 hours on certain transfers to foreign platforms or self-custody wallets as part of new measures aimed at preventing fraud.
On Friday, the Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) said the requirement will apply to funds received above $10,000, either in a single transaction or based on a customer’s total transactions in a day. Providers must also hold other transfers requiring further scrutiny under their risk-management policies.
The rules take effect on Jan. 1, 2027. Providers must notify customers of holds and keep records of fraud incidents, attempted fraud and corrective actions. A VASP may complete its assessment and release a transfer before the 24 hours expire, provided that it follows parameters set out by the central bank.
The measure adds Brazil to a growing list of jurisdictions tightening crypto safeguards as regulators confront scams that exploit the speed and cross-border reach of digital assets.
Brazil joins global push against crypto scams
Brazil’s move follows anti-scam measures introduced in other jurisdictions. In Japan, the Financial Services Agency and National Police Agency asked crypto exchanges to restrict withdrawals after customers deposit fiat currency or buy digital assets.
The authorities also called for platforms to require customers to preregister withdrawal addresses and impose a waiting period before newly added addresses can be used.
Other proposed safeguards include customer-specific withdrawal limits, stronger monitoring, phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and checks that the name of a bank remitter matches the crypto account holder.
Unlike Brazil’s regulation, the Japanese measures are not binding. In addition, exchanges can determine implementation based on their operations and exposure to misuse.
Related: Brazil bars crypto settlement in regulated cross-border payment rails
European regulators have warned of criminals impersonating watchdogs and crypto companies as users search for licensed service providers after the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets licensing deadline.
France’s financial regulator reported cases involving fake websites, while the European Securities and Markets Authority said scammers had misused its identity and logo in falsified documents.

title: 8 Best Workout Headphones & Earbuds: Beats, Bose, Apple (2026)
summary: Not every great pair of headphones belongs in the gym. These do, thanks to their secure fit, durable design, and impeccable sound.
full_text:
The best workout headphones disappear when you start moving. They’re locked in without readjustments and comfortable enough that the music feels like it’s coming from inside your head. Your workout headphones have a tougher job than your everyday pair. They need to survive sweat, being thrown into a gym bag, and the occasional drop. They also need to sound good enough to keep you motivated until the finish line.
The WIRED Reviews team has tested hundreds of headphones and earbuds, and I’ve narrowed down the models that best balance sound quality, comfort, and durability. We put these picks through workouts like weightlifting and indoor swimming, as well as outdoor activities like trail runs, hikes, and cycling, to evaluate which headphones enhanced the experience and which ones got in the way. This roundup includes a mix of headphones and earbuds, wired and wireless, from the top pick, the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 ($250), to the bone-conduction Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 ($180).
For more recommendations, check out our guides to the Best Wireless Earbuds, the Best Open Earbuds, and the Best Bone Conduction Headphones.
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Featured in This Guide
Best Wireless Earbuds for Working Out
Beats were the first sport earbuds to tap into Apple’s ecosystem, but the Powerbeats Pro 2 work nearly as well with Android, making them a great pick for any phone. The redesigned nickel-titanium ear hooks stayed in place through hours of testing, and former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata said they’re the most comfortable hooked earbuds he’s worn. The noise canceling is a major upgrade, outperforming the Beats Studio Buds+ and holding its own against premium rivals like Sony’s WF-1000XM5 and Technics’ AZ80. The Powerbeats Pro 2 also finally add a natural-sounding transparency mode, along with punchy sound, up to 10 hours of battery life (eight with ANC enabled), and convenient push-button controls.
Apple users get extras like iCloud device switching, Find My functionality, and hands-free Siri, while Android users still benefit from the Beats app, heart rate monitoring, and one-touch pairing. I wish the PowerBeats Pro 2 had a higher IP rating than IPX4, but they’re still built to handle sweat and light rain.
Best Wireless Headphones for Working Out
If you prefer over-ear headphones for your workouts, the Bose QuietComfort Ultra 2 are hard to beat. The plush fit is comfortable enough for long listening sessions, and the impressive noise canceling blocks out any distractions at the gym. The sound is clear and engaging, with plenty of punch, plus a transparency mode that feels natural. Bose also added useful upgrades like USB-C lossless audio, improved ambient controls, and longer battery life.
The ear cups do trap heat and sweat, but I have yet to find a pair of over-ear headphones that don't encourage sweat during intense workouts. Nonetheless, they are a premium pick for anyone who wants workout headphones to double as everyday headphones.
Best Budget Buds
JLab’s Go Air Sport is the sport version of the insanely affordable Go Air, with a slight markup for over-ear hooks and a case with a cover. That case also has a built-in USB charger. The build quality is solid, and touch controls are not too sensitive; I don't accidentally turn off my music or turn up the volume whenever I adjust my hair or my hat. They have a solid 30 hours of battery life when you recharge them in the case. I wore them for two weeks for a few hours each day while running and walking my dog, and I didn't have to recharge them once. And the Bluetooth connection is stronger than most affordable earbuds I've tried; I don't have to be wary about walking around a corner, away from my phone. As a bonus, they also come in a wide array of playful colors. —Adrienne So
Best Premium Earbuds
Bose is the undisputed king of noise-canceling headphones, so if you really need to lock in, consider the QuietComfort Ultra 2 Earbuds. According to former editor Parker Hall, the noise-canceling on the second-gen pair bested the competition and was better than its predecessor. You get wireless charging in the clamshell and guards to prevent earwax buildup. Bose uses a chiming calibration tool to adjust the sound profile and noise-canceling response to the shape of your actual ear canals, which is impressive. If you get too deep in the zone, there's also an Aware mode that lets you hear ambient noise while smoothing out loud sounds. Not only are these the best for the gym, but they're also probably the best pair for anyone who wants noise cancellation in a compact package that you can tote around every day. —Adrienne So
Best Earbuds for Apple Users
The AirPods Pro 3 are the first AirPods model I've used that I legitimately consider to be workout headphones. (Previous models fell out all the time.) Apple conducted what former WIRED editor Parker Hall calls “an ungodly number” of laser ear scans, and there is a greater choice of ear tips. The XXS small tips actually fit me well, and these are the first AirPods Pros that haven't fallen out of my ears while running.
Like the Powerbeats Pro 2, they also have heart rate sensing, so if you're tracking your workout with Fitness+ and using Workout Buddy, you can see your live heart rate in the app or on your Apple Watch. Noise canceling is also excellent if you're working out in the gym. Apple's bass-heavy, bright tuning is also ideal if you're bopping around to pop sensations like Haim or Mariah Carey when you're working out. —Adrienne So
Best Earbuds for Running
The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 now charge via USB-C, so you can say goodbye to their proprietary charger. These earbuds use both air and bone conduction to transmit sound while you’re working out outside. This new model added a second air-conduction unit, which improves the sound quality and reduces the tingling sensation you get with bone conduction.
WIRED contributing reviewer Michael Sawh notes that the battery life is slightly less than promised, and the waterproof rating is lower than on previous iterations (IP67). According to Sawh, the sound quality isn’t as clear as one might like, but the bass and punch are still powerful. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So says these are her favorite pair of headphones for cycling because they fit comfortably underneath a helmet.
Best Earbuds for Swimming
The OpenSwim Pro has an industry-leading IP68 rating and a dedicated swimming EQ mode that produces a balanced sound that is pleasant to listen to underwater. According to WIRED contributing reviewer Michael Sawh, the controls are easy to use, and the neckband is slim enough to wear under a swim cap. Since Bluetooth doesn’t work underwater, you’ll need to import audio files from your computer onto your swim headphones. There’s 32 GB of onboard storage. Be sure to check the format to make sure it's compatible; the OpenSwim Pro supports MP3, FLAC, WAV, AAC, M4A, APE, and WMA files.
Best Wired Earbuds for Working Out
If you're running or hiking, it's convenient to have a pair of earbuds that are attached to you and won't fall into a puddle. Former WIRED editor Adrienne So loves these Soundpeats Q40HD, mainly because they’re designed with two clips to attach to your shirt; plus the buds themselves are magnetic and click together when not in use. In testing, Adrienne was able to get around 20 hours of battery life, and even when power is low, a quick top-off with a USB-C cable got her more than enough battery to last for an hour-long trail run. The headphones don't include active noise cancellation, but they fit well enough to provide passive noise cancellation. They block ambient sounds so well, in fact, that she only wears one bud when running.
Honorable Mentions

title: These AI Barons Are Ready to Give Away Their Fortunes
summary: A new generation of philanthropists made rich by artificial intelligence are preparing to give away their vast wealth. What should we make of a multi-billion-dollar pinky promise?
full_text:
David Silver is a billionaire, sort of. His stake in Ineffable Intelligence—the artificial intelligence lab he founded—is worth an ungodly fortune. But he stands to collect none of that money himself. He set things up that way.
Between 2013 and 2025, Silver worked as a researcher at Google DeepMind. He specialized in reinforcement learning, a method of teaching an AI model through positive and negative feedback. In 2016, he led the development of AlphaGo, which became the first AI to defeat a human champion in the game of Go and was heralded as a narrow form of superintelligence. Silver left to start Ineffable Intelligence in January, betting that reinforcement learning breakthroughs will close the gap between human and machine cognition across the board.
When he started Ineffable Intelligence, Silver raised $1.1 billion from investors at a $5.1 billion valuation, reportedly the largest seed round in Europe’s history. He also vowed to donate all the money he makes from any future sale of his company to charity.
“I was thinking very deeply about what I could do to have the maximum impact on the world,” Silver tells WIRED in an interview at his office in Kings Cross, London, around the corner from DeepMind’s headquarters. “Not just through the work I do, but through the finance I arrive at in the process.”
He’ll choose how to deploy the funds after he sells his company, he says, but his ambition is to save as many lives as possible.
Silver is the latest in a growing line of AI founders to pledge equity proceeds to charity. Others include Mustafa Suleyman, a DeepMind cofounder and the CEO of AI at Microsoft, and Anton Osika, the founder of automated coding platform Lovable. If OpenAI and Anthropic go public as planned, minting thousands of new millionaires in the process, the AI industry could soon come to represent an increasingly outsize proportion of tech philanthropy.
Along with a new generation of techno-philanthropists, though, comes a tangle of unresolved questions: Is philanthropy the most appropriate way to redistribute wealth? To what degree are megadonors responsible for some of the problems they aim to fix? Could a pledge that scales with a company’s success come to justify unsavory business practices or reckless accelerationism? And is this go-around any different from previous iterations of Silicon Valley giving?
“You can’t necessarily appeal to capitalism to solve some of the problems created by capitalist practices themselves … the exacerbation of extreme wealth concentration and massive inequalities,” says Linsey McGoey, professor of sociology at the University of Essex and author of No Such Thing as a Free Gift. “It’s like calling upon the arsonist to hose down the house he’s just set on fire.”
Silver formalized his charitable commitment through Founders Pledge, a nonprofit that helps entrepreneurs to give away their wealth. Unlike the Giving Pledge, a public but nonbinding commitment, Founders Pledge requires participants to enter into a contract. “The choice of making a binding pledge was very important,” says Silver.
Founders Pledge has been around since 2015. But the value of pledges recorded by the nonprofit has soared recently, from $400 million in 2023 to $4 billion so far this year. The AI industry now accounts for a third of the lifetime pledge total.
The organization’s goal, according to cofounder David Goldberg, is to identify “the very best ways to deploy capital at scale to make the world better.” It has frequently been lumped together with effective altruism, which encourages people to amass wealth in order to give it away, to rely on statistics rather than emotion, and to prioritize causes likely to have the biggest impact in the distant future. But despite the commonalities, Goldberg isn’t a fan of the comparison; Founders Pledge is concerned with human suffering in the present. “We’re far more humanist,” he says.
Silver considers himself an effective altruist but says his “flavor is about the here and now.” Accordingly, Silver plans to funnel his pledge proceeds to charities, like the Malaria Foundation, equipped to save the greatest number of lives in the near term. “I find it hard to justify focusing on the galactic future of humanity when there are millions of people suffering and dying today,” he says.
Osika, the Lovable founder, who has pledged to give away half of his equity proceeds, doesn’t identify as an effective altruist, but he shares the belief that amassing wealth by succeeding in business is the best way for him to maximize his personal impact on the world. “I think it’s a very good thing for people who are very thoughtful about the future of humanity to build [AI],” he tells WIRED.
The Gates Foundation—the most famous embodiment of techno-philanthropy—has given away more than $100 billion to causes targeting poverty and disease in the 25 years since it was founded by Bill and Melinda Gates. Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, have pledged to donate their $200 billion fortune to scientific research through their own foundation, the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Both have been held up as shining examples of how an entrepreneurial mindset can translate into effective philanthropy and how the profit motive can be harnessed for good.
The new generation of AI philanthropists appear to want to carry that legacy forward, into a world they imagine will be utterly reorganized by superintelligence. “For a very long time, it’s been clear to me that this technological transformation is going to be the biggest thing that happens in our lives,” says Osika.
However, this type of giving can come with trade-offs, and can be used by megadonors to discreetly advance their political interests, McGoey says. A recent study found that a reliance on philanthropic funding led the WHO to prioritize donors’ preferred causes at the expense of other urgent issues, like non-communicable diseases.
Donations that alleviate issues stemming from wealth inequality instead of attacking the root cause, McGoey argues, threaten to end the debate about long-term, systemic remedies before it begins. “It’s appealing to the perpetuator of a problem to resolve it—and that doesn’t necessarily lead to positive results,” she says. “I don’t think that people should kid themselves that making money on its own is somehow noble.”
The WHO itself has acknowledged issues with its financing, and in 2022 it put forth a new model designed to address some of those concerns. Mark Suzman, the Gates Foundation’s CEO, has also recognized the pitfalls of relying on megadonors. “It’s not right for a private philanthropy to be one of the largest funders of multinational global health efforts,” he said in 2023, noting that the foundation had become the WHO’s second-largest donor. But he also put the blame on dwindling governmental contributions. “I’d love it if many more governments would pass us on that list,” he said.
Megadonors can play a valuable role in funding causes neglected for ideological reasons by governments, like family planning. But they’re not equally accountable, says Apolline Taillandier, a researcher at the University of Cambridge who specializes in political theory. “These funders are not elected. They have no need to account for their decisions,” she says. “It comes down to the question of whether philanthropy is the most legitimate way of redistributing resources.”
There is a further risk that entrepreneurs might treat their philanthropic ambition as moral justification for destructive behavior. In 2024, the one-time crypto kingpin and effective altruism poster boy Sam Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison for fraud. At trial, a former colleague testified that Bankman-Fried had based all of his decisions on cold statistical analysis, gladly risking disaster if it meant a chance at a sufficiently positive end result. The leaders of effective altruism declared Bankman-Friend an apostate, but others painted his frau

title: 比特幣 BIP-110 分叉只挖 2 個區塊就卡死，先鋒礦工 Roughnecks 宣布放棄
summary:
BIP-110 分叉鏈最鮮明的旗手 Roughnecks 宣布停止挖礦，坦言分裂鏈已陷入停滯。分裂以來，BIP […]

〈比特幣 BIP-110 分叉只挖 2 個區塊就卡死，先鋒礦工 Roughnecks 宣布放棄〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
BIP-110 分叉鏈最鮮明的旗手 Roughnecks 宣布停止挖礦，坦言分裂鏈已陷入停滯。分裂以來，BIP-110 鏈僅多挖出一個區塊便卡死，信號支持率僅 2.53%，離 55% 鎖定門檻相去甚遠。
（前情提要：比特幣今晨軟分叉！BIP-110 支持者跑少數鏈，主網已甩開 26 區塊）
（背景補充：比特幣「內戰」落幕？BIP-110 敵意收購嘗試，目前支持算力連 1% 都不到）
BIP-110 陣營最前線的礦工，Roughnecks 於台灣時間今（9）日中午在 X 發文宣布停止挖礦，並呼籲所有還在現行演算法下挖 BIP-110 鏈的人停手。少了這支先鋒部隊，原本就奄奄一息的少數鏈，等於失去最後一絲脈動。
A few minutes ago at 0340 UTC we had a team meeting and made the difficult decision to stop mining operations under the name Roughnecks. This decision did not come lightly. We do not see this a defeat for the BIP110 movement but an escalation to the next step. Anyone who is…
— Roughnecks (@Roughnecks110) August 9, 2026
分裂 8 小時就卡死
比特幣主鏈與 BIP-110 鏈的分家，起於區塊高度 961,632（台灣時間今日清晨挖出），BIP-110 為期兩週的「強制信號」窗口正式開啟。
礦池 AntPool 挖出一個未帶 BIP-110 信號的 961,632 區塊，主鏈照單全收；但執行 BIP-110 規則的節點拒絕承認這個區塊，轉而跟隨 Roughnecks 透過 Ocean 礦池在同一高度挖出的替代區塊，兩條鏈自此正式分道揚鑣。
問題是，BIP-110 鏈從此再也追不上。鏈上資料顯示，這條少數鏈分裂後只多挖出 961,633 一個區塊，然後就陷入停滯；反觀主鏈一路推進。
算力對比更是懸殊。分裂前的 2,016 個區塊中，只有 51 個信號支持 BIP-110，比例僅 2.53%，離鎖定門檻 55%（等同 1,109 個區塊）差了一大截。更致命的是難度：961,632 那一刻難度剛好調整到 127.48 兆，少數鏈繼承了與主鏈相同的難度，算力卻只剩零頭。
有監測站估算，BIP-110 鏈要撐到下一次難度調整得走完約 350 天，主鏈只要 14 天就能完成同樣的循環。強制信號窗口將在區塊 963,647 截止，若要成功鎖定必須在 963,648 達標，規則正式生效則要等到 965,664，試行期涵蓋 52,416 個區塊，約一年。
BIP-110 的規則與時間表
BIP-110 由匿名開發者 Dathon Ohm 撰寫，正式名稱為「Reduced Data Temporary Soft fork」（削減資料臨時軟分叉）。它提出一系列為期約一年的共識層限制，目標是抑制比特幣鏈上的非金融資料儲存：
- 限制多數新輸出指令碼為 34 位元組
- OP_RETURN 輸出上限 83 位元組
- 限制部分資料推送與 witness 元素為 256 位元組
- 暫時限制若干 Taproot 功能
- 啟用前已建立未花費的交易輸出（UTXO）豁免
這些限制將在 block 965,664 正式生效，持續 52,416 個區塊（約一年）後自動解除。
批評陣營：這會傷到比特幣
BIP-110 的批評者早就警告這條路線會導致分裂。Blockstream 共同創辦人 Adam Back 在 X 平台直言：「這根本行不通，破壞多項機制，沒有技術共識也沒有生態系共識，四樣致命缺陷全都有。大家都討厭垃圾資料，但這不是方法，你們會傷到自己。」
比特幣安全專家 Jameson Lopp 發布了詳細分析，稱 BIP-110「魯莽且註定失敗」，指出分裂風險、可能產生無法花費的 UTXO（Taproot 邊緣情況）、長期無法真正阻止資料儲存（可以用其他方式嵌入），以及對錢包、Miniscript 工具和預簽名交易的相容性負擔。
微策略執行董事長 Michael Saylor 今年 7 月發表一篇 110 點的論述反對 BIP-110，核心論點是共識規則應處理已證明存在的威脅，而非交易者的「感知目的」。他寫道：「比特幣不需要純度的守護者，需要的是中立的守護者。」

title: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan to be returned to Ireland in high-security operation
summary: The Irish Prison Service bought a bulletproof and bomb-proof van to transport the 49-year-old to court after his extradition from Dubai.
full_text:
Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan to be returned to Ireland in high-security operation
- Published
A large-scale security operation is in place in the Republic of Ireland as the authorities prepare for the extradition of alleged crime boss Daniel Kinahan.
The 49-year-old was arrested in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in April and on Saturday an Irish government jet flew to Dubai to prepare to collect him.
The plane is expected to return to Dublin on Sunday and Kinahan will then be taken to the Special Criminal Court.
Ahead of the extradition, the Irish Prison Service bought a bulletproof and bombproof van which can be used to escort prisoners who are considered high-risk.
Irish authorities are expected to prosecute him for his involvement in leading an organised crime group.
Kinahan is not only wanted by the authorities in Ireland - the US Treasury Department once described the Kinahan cartel as one of the most dangerous in the world.
The US government imposed sanctions on Kinahan in April 2022 after he and other members of his family were identified as leaders of the Kinahan organised crime cartel.
He fought attempts to extradite him back to his native country, where the Kinahan cartel was involved in a long-running gangland feud that claimed 18 lives.
Kinahan himself became a target for murder and escaped an attempt on his life during a fatal shooting at a Dublin hotel in 2016.
He left Ireland and spent time living in Spain and more recently in Dubai, where a warrant for his arrest was issued by the Irish courts in April.
He appealed the extradition order over the past few months but his attempts were unsuccessful.
It is expected that shortly after his arrival in Ireland he will be taken to the non-jury Special Criminal Court in Dublin to face charges for alleged involvement in leading an organised crime group.
Sunday's security operation will involve armed gardaí (Irish police) and members of the Irish Defence Forces as well as the Irish Prison Service, according RTÉ News.
The broadcaster also said facilities have been upgraded in the maximum-security Portlaoise Prison in County Laois where he is expected to be held on remand.
An extradition agreement is in place between the UAE and Ireland and it was used to extradite Sean McGovern, a "senior lieutenant" in the organised crime group.
He was sentenced to 24 years in prison in June for directing the activities of a criminal organisation.
What is the Kinahan cartel?
For more than 20 years the group has been responsible for importing tonnes of drugs and firearms around the world, the National Crime Agency (NCA) previously said.
The NCA said the crime group is linked to more than a dozen gangland murders.
According to former Gardaí (Irish police) Commissioner Drew Harris, the gang is estimated to have made more than €1bn (£836,590,000) globally from its activities.
The US Treasury Department has in the past compared the gang to crime organisations such as Italy's Camorra, Mexico's Los Zetas and Japan's Yakuza.
A reward of up to $5m (£3.84m) has also been offered by the US for information on the three most senior Kinahan gang members - Daniel, his father Christopher Snr, 65, and brother Christopher Jnr.
In 2022, Thomas Kavanagh, who the NCA said ran the group's criminal operations in the UK, was jailed for 21 years alongside Gary Vickery and Daniel Canning, who were sentenced to 20 years and 19 and a half years respectively.
The NCA said evidence showed they were responsible for cocaine imports estimated to be up to £23.4m, and cannabis imports worth about £6.4m.
Daniel Kinahan's lawyer previously told BBC Panorama that he has no criminal record or convictions and allegations about him being a crime boss are false and have no evidential basis.
