title: 'Not afraid to stay': The Canadians taking fighting wildfires into their own hands
summary: With wildfires now widespread and frequent, some rural residents in Canada are learning how to fight the flames themselves and protect their own homes.
full_text:
'Not afraid to stay': The Canadians taking fighting wildfires into their own hands
- Published
When a wildfire broke out near his First Nation community in northern Ontario, Hubert Wigwas decided to stay put.
He put sprinklers on his roof to extinguish falling embers. He checked on elders in his community who also stayed behind, and he fuelled up four boats down on the lake in case they needed a quick escape.
"This is everything I've built in my 58 years," Wigwas, a councillor from Gull Bay First Nation, told the BBC. "I'm just not going to run away and let it burn."
Canada has seen some of its worst fire seasons in recent years, and experienced its most destructive on record in 2023, when blazes tore through forest land roughly the size of Syria. As of this August, more than 750 wildfires are actively burning across the country.
The impact has been felt as far as the US Midwest, where smoke had choked the air in cities. Even President Donald Trump has taken note, threatening to further tariff Canada for allowing "filthy, polluted" air to waft south of the border.
The intensifying wildfires have sparked a national conversation: Are there enough firefighters to battle these more challenging fire seasons? What happens when resources are stretched too thin? And how can remote communities, often closest to danger because of their proximity to Canada's vast boreal forest, learn to live with this new reality?
Wigwas asked himself these questions when he decided to stay, even as he faces a fine of around C$800 ($570; £425) for defying evacuation orders.
Leaders of Gull Bay First Nation, also known as Kiashke Zaaging Anishinaabek, have been urging residents to stay away since mid-July as more than 150 wildfires burn across Ontario's northwest.
Its chief penned a letter on 29 July pleading with those who have remained to leave immediately, saying that Ontario firefighters cannot do their jobs safely with people still in their homes.
It is the same message officials across the country have been conveying in British Columbia, where around 115 fires are currently burning.
But with a wildfire 24km outside his community, Wigwas, speaking in late July, said he had yet to see fire personnel from out of town there to help fireproof properties or keep an eye out on the elders who remained.
He said it made him realise that his First Nation would benefit from setting up its own wildfire emergency response and teaching residents how to protect their own homes.
"Everybody talks about climate change, but nobody is doing something to unite the (First Nations) reserves and have a system like that set up," Wigwas said.
Dave Bradley, a spokesperson for Ontario's ministry of natural resources, did not address Wigwas' claim directly, but said the province has been in "constant contact" with First Nations leaders.
He added that fire fighting resources are directed based on "fire behaviour, weather conditions and risks to communities."
In the west-coast province of British Columbia - long the front line of Canada's wildfire response - people are doing just what Wigwas is envisioning for his First Nation, with efforts underway to train residents of rural and remote communities how to safely respond to wildfires before out-of-town crews can arrive.
Sonja Leverkus, a wildfire researcher and specialist, said she has helped train more than 400 people in and around her community of Fort Nelson over the last three years through a firefighting group she helped start called the Northeast BC Rural Incident Management Team.
She told the BBC that her efforts are inspired by a realisation that Canada needs to change how it fights wildfires as climate change increases their frequency and intensity.
"There are not enough human beings in Canada," she said, with the appropriate training, "to fight the fires that we have currently, especially over the last five years".
Remote communities, where the nearest town might be hundreds of kilometres away, can sometimes be bumped down the priority list for BC firefighting crews if there are blazes threatening more populated areas, she said.
Her crew, who are primarily indigenous, have carried out prescribed burns, also known as a hazard reduction burns – a practice of setting planned, controlled blazes to remove fuels that could contribute to wildfires.
They have also helped put out smaller fires before they grow out of control using fire wagons that they purchased through fundraising and grants, sometimes arriving ahead of provincial firecrews and then working in tandem with them, Leverkus said.
When a major wildfire tore through Fort Nelson in 2024, she said she and 40 of her team members stayed behind and were hired by the province to clear flammables and support fire suppression activities.
Leverkus also organised a structural protection training course for locals to learn how to shield buildings from embers that can quickly spur fires that engulf entire towns.
"We have mechanics, we have carpenters, we have real good problem solvers," Leverkus said. "We're all not afraid to stay."
Cam Allen, a 70-year-old former helicopter pilot in Fort Nelson who has previously fought fires from the air, said he recently took Leverkus' course to learn about ground fire suppression techniques, and, more broadly, how to help if a blaze reaches his town.
He mentioned John Carr, a California man who went viral last year, external for staying behind and warding off flames with a garden hose during the Palisades fire, ultimately saving his home even when others around it burned down.
"It makes you wonder, if 100 people had stayed or 1,000 people had stayed behind and actually did what he did, how much more could have been saved?" Allen asked.
But not all were as fortunate as Carr during the Los Angeles fires, which killed a total of 29 people – a few of whom had, too, defied evacuation orders in order to protect their homes, even as officials urged thousands in the area to leave.
Leverkus' group is not officially recognised by BC's government, and what it is trying to achieve highlights simmering tensions in fire-prone regions between those who enforce evacuation orders and those who defy them.
Last week, wildfire crews in BC were forced to rescue a man when his home in the Village of Clinton was surrounded by flames, after he had refused to evacuate.
In a wildfire update on Tuesday, BC's minister responsible for emergency management reiterated that all those who are under evacuation orders should leave.
"We may not be able to get back to you if an emergency happens," warned Minister Kelly Greene, adding that evacuation orders are made as "a last resort to keep people and communities safe".
Paul Kovacs, a researcher at the University of Western Ontario and director of its Catastrophic Loss Reduction Institute, said that Canada has had a lower fatality rate from wildfires despite their frequency in part because of its evacuation approach.
The stay and defend mindset, he said, "is aggressively opposed" by the academic community in Canada, as opposed to other fire-prone countries like Australia.
"In the hierarchy of what is it that you do to manage a wildfire, preservation of life is first," Kovacs said.
Rural and remote communities can and should play an outsized role in informing officials of how best to protect their town, he said, and can do a lot of work to fire proof homes and structures. But that work, he argued, should not be done "while the fire is burning."
A spokesperson for BC's Ministry of Forests told the BBC that self-organised groups in rural areas can be hired temporarily by the province during an active wildfire, but only when there are no more available provincial firefighters in the area.
The ministry added that BC Wildfire's full-time staff has increased by 56% in recent years to respond to the growing frequency of fires, in addition to seasonal staff.

title: 'Roll on 2027' as Fleadh 2026 in Belfast comes to an end
summary: The 2026 festival was being hosted in the city for the first time and ended on Sunday.
full_text:
'Roll on 2027' as Fleadh 2026 comes to an end
- Published
The first All Ireland Fleadh in Belfast ended in the early hours of Monday morning with organisers saying they were overwhelmed by the positive response they received from all communities.
It is estimated that there were more than a million people in the city centre during the eight days of the fleadh.
At least 4,000 were still in the grounds of Belfast City Hall at 01:00 BST to hear the closing speeches and final tunes.
Niall McClean, co-chair of the organising committee, told the crowd they were all part of an historic event.
He said: "We've done something that has never, ever happened in this city before. We've brought every single community together – and everybody has absolutely loved it."
McClean added that it has "put a permanent smile on my face. I'm the happiest man in Belfast. Roll on 2027".
"What an incredible week. Everyone I have spoken to has had an amazing time here in Belfast, thousands of people all on a high.
"Belfast has shone, the world has come to our doorstep, bringing the biggest numbers ever seen for a Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann.
"I'm so proud of our branch and all our members, and what we have achieved together. We dared to dream and those dreams have come true."
To loud applause, he ended by saying: "Well done Belfast, we'll see you next year."
The All Ireland Fleadh returns to the city from 1 to 8 August 2027.
Dr Labhrás Ó Murchú, director general of Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann (society of the musicians of Ireland) which runs the annual All Ireland Fleadh, described this year's festival as a "miracle."
He told the crowd: "I hope that when you go back (home), you'll bring with you not just the memories but you'll tell people that you were part of - and you witnessed and you experienced - a miracle here in Belfast this week.
"Because it was a miracle, a miracle of music, a miracle of friendship, a miracle of creativity."
The final performance of the night came from Lissadell Céilí Band, winners of the senior Céilí band competition.
Earlier performances included Belfast-based Campbell College Bugles, Pipes and Drums and Bangor singer Foy Vance.
Lord Mayor of Belfast councillor Róis-Máire Donnelly officially brought the fleadh to a close.
The eight-day event was jointly hosted by Belfast City Council, Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann (CCE) and Ards CCÉ.
Donnelly, said: "Words cannot do justice to how proud I am of this city and the magic that it has produced over the last eight days.
"Our spirit, our craic and our shared love of music, from all our different communities, have all been embraced and displayed for everyone to enjoy."
She described the event as a "watershed moment" adding: "A sign of our city's strength, ambition and future potential. Fleadh 2026 has surpassed all of our expectations."
John Walsh, Chief Executive of Belfast City Council, said bringing the Fleadh to the city "has been a long time in the making".
"Seeing it come to life on our streets this past week will live long in the memory.
"Whether you volunteered, performed or became a proud tourist in your hometown, your support, co-operation and positivity have all been essential in making the event such a huge success – I hope to see you all at the Fleadh again, 1-8 August 2027."
Dr Labhrás O Murchú from CCÉ said the event was "unprecedented".
"Belfast opened its doors and hearts to the multitudes who came from far and near for this amazing celebration, which will have an encore in 2027.
"One million fans can say to Belfast 'you are the envy of the world', with perhaps billions worldwide aware of the cultural history made in August 2026."
Calls for city centre to be pedestrianised
The success of the Fleadh has prompted calls for Belfast city centre to be pedestrianised permanently.
A large zone in the city centre was created over the course of the festival.
Representatives from the Alliance Party from across Belfast have now written to the council and other bodies calling for a "comprehensive review of pedestrianisation" in the city centre.
South Belfast MLA Kate Nicholl said the Fleadh showed "Belfast at its best, open, welcoming and full of life".
"When we design our streets around people instead of traffic, our city centre becomes somewhere people actually want to spend time, and that's good for our shops, our hospitality sector and as we've seen so clearly this week, our sense of civic pride".
She said accessibility had to be taken seriously, however.
"Any expansion has to be designed with disabled people and accessibility organisations from the start, not bolted on afterwards. That means looking properly at disabled parking, accessible drop-off points, public transport connectivity and wayfinding," she said.
Green Party councillor Brian Smyth said the "bottom line" is that the Fleadh "would not have worked without pedestrianisation in the city centre".
"I think it is starting a conversation with people," he said.
"This isn't some new, radical idea."
However disability campaign groups, such as Disabled People Against Cuts Northern Ireland (DPAC NI), have voiced concern.
On social media they said: "We've seen this played out elsewhere and it's disabled people who pay a price for 'progress'."
DPAC NI spokesperson Dermot Devlin said that "many disabled people can only walk or wheel short distances".
"We need to park or get off public transport close to our destinations."
He added that "further pedestrianisation" of the city centre "without significant mitigation will exclude many of us from our city".
"We have a right to access the city on an equal basis to everyone else. Like everyone else we use the city centre as a place to shop, a place to work and place to go out in.
"Agencies involved in making permanent or temporary changes to the city centre must uphold our rights, not ignore them."

title: 'Body in suitcase' found in Australia turns out to be lifelike doll
summary: Forensics revealed that the 'realistic' looking body was in fact not human.
full_text:
'Body in suitcase' found in Australia turns out to be lifelike doll
- Published
Australian police called in to investigate a body found in a suitcase have concluded that the "victim" was in fact a lifelike doll.
The suitcase was discovered by two men on the side of a road near the small village of Oallen, about 230km (143 miles) south-west of Sydney.
On Monday, police announced a murder investigation, sparking intense interest in the case but backtracked hours later, saying forensic testing had proved the contents were not human.
The contents in the suitcase were "mistaken for a human originally, so they are very realistic in terms of looking like human remains," said Supt Linda Bradbury from the Hume Police District.
"But we've confirmed by other means that they are not."
The doll was wearing clothing, had hair and a nose piercing," police said, adding that "the item also had markings that resembled bruises and grazes".
Supt Bradbury said forensic teams and investigators had attended the scene on Sunday and that all processes had been followed.
"The idea is to not disturb crime scenes as much as possible, to maintain the integrity of our investigation," Bradbury said, adding she had "no regrets" about how the case was handled.
Hours earlier, Bradbury had told media that it has been "quite a shocking discovery" for the two men who found the suitcase.
"Unfortunately, they were on a weekend drive as a lot of people do over the weekend and stopped for a break," she said.
She said the pair had made the "right decision" to report the find.
"They were affected yesterday and we will be in touch to let them know that it was not human remains," Bradbury said.
Police have now closed their investigations.

full_text:
Chinese researchers use microbubbles to shrink aggressive liver tumours: paper
Cancer patients who received the experimental treatment in combination with standard therapies saw improvement, study finds
Chinese researchers have found a safe way to shrink advanced tumours from an aggressive form of liver cancer, an advance that could see microbubbles used to enhance current treatments.
The tiny gas-filled bubbles, typically a few micrometres in diameter, were originally designed as contrast agents in ultrasound imaging, but scientists have recently been exploring their therapeutic potential.
According to a paper published by the peer-reviewed Scientific Reports on July 19, the study compared cancer patients who received the standard therapy with a group that also received the experimental ultrasound and microbubble treatment.
The researchers, from the Affiliated Hospital of Guangdong Medical University and Huzhou Central Hospital, found that tumours in the second group of patients grew smaller than in those who only received the standard therapy.
“This technology shows [promise] for enhancing localised treatment approaches in cancer patients,” they wrote in the reviewed but unedited manuscript, which was provided with legal disclaimers to give early access to the findings, according to the journal.
Microbubbles are used in various fields, including engineering, environmental clean-up, and medicine. When injected into the bloodstream and hit by ultrasound waves, these bubbles can expand or contract.

full_text:
A “preconceived plan” to do harm at a party has resulted in a young man’s death and murder charges for eight teenagers, police say.
The group of teens allegedly attended an Airbnb gathering south of Brisbane armed with various weapons before it erupted into violence and left the 21-year-old man with catastrophic head injuries.
He was gravely injured after the party at the rented home in Bahrs Scrub, a suburb of Logan, on 26 July, Det Insp Ian Galpin told reporters on Monday.
‘‘A 21-year-old Redbank Plains man was located in an unconscious state, suffering head injuries,’’ he said.
He was transported to hospital in a critical condition and died six days later.
A group of young men have been accused of arming themselves before they arrived at the party which left several vehicles destroyed, a home extensively damaged and a street shut down, police said.
‘‘The police will allege that this group had a preconceived plan, which included arming themselves with various weapons before attending Bahrs Scrub with the common purpose of inflicting harm on persons at that address,’’ Galpin said.
The fatal attack triggered a major homicide investigation.
‘‘More than 80 police were involved in the execution of 14 search warrants across three police districts,’’ Galpin said.
Four teens were initially charged with murder on 6 August – two 18-year-olds and two 19-year-olds.
Another four were located and charged on Sunday – a 17-year-old and three 18-year-olds.
“Our investigations have continued, and [on Sunday] … we located an additional four persons at short-term accommodation in Morayfield, and those persons were also arrested and charged with murder,” Galpin said.
Police have warned more arrests are possible.
‘‘It is an ongoing investigation, so that is a possibility. If we identify more persons involved in this offence, then they will be charged.’’
Police liaison officers and community leaders have been working to prevent any retaliation.
‘‘Everyone that we have spoken to, they want nothing but peace within their community, and that’s why I’m confident there won’t be any further retaliation,’’ Galpin said.
‘‘We’ll continue to support the community, and we’ll also continue to deliver our message that any form of violence will not be tolerated.’’
Galpin praised the response from local residents, saying community cooperation had been “nothing short of amazing”.
‘‘If not for this cooperation, I don’t think we’d be in the position that we’re here in today and I think it highlights the importance of police working with the community and vice versa to solve these serious crimes.’’

Good morning. In late July, Itamar Ben-Gvir, West Bank settler and far-right extremist minister of security in Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, joined a group of more than 2,000 Jewish extremists to storm al-Aqsa mosque compound, Jerusalem’s most sensitive holy site. The far-right group has been doing this for years. Ben-Gvir has made series of visits to the site over the last three years, eroding norms and inflaming tensions. Jordanian officials have recently warned that it could be at risk of an “imminent” Israeli takeover.
With national elections scheduled in October, and many eyes still firmly on Gaza (this weekend, Netanyahu rejected a US-backed 15 point plan for peace), the Israeli government appears to be racing to expand Israeli settlements and accelerate ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in the West Bank and East Jerusalem before its mandate expires.
For this morning’s First Edition, I spoke to our senior international correspondent, Julian Borger, about the latest incursions, and how Israeli extremists are trying to create a new reality in Jerusalem. That’s after the weekend roundup.
Weekend roundup
- 
  UK politics | Sadiq Khan has called on the government to commit to revamped climate action and to reduce the UK’s reliance on oil and gas, as the UK endures a summer of drought, wildfires and heatwaves.
- 
  US politics | The US Senate voted to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general in a win for Donald Trump, who will now have his one-time personal attorney sitting atop the nation’s law enforcement apparatus.

- 
  World news | The alleged leader of the Kinahan organised crime group was extradited from Dubai on Sunday and met by a huge security operation in Dublin, marking the end of a global game of cat and mouse with European, US and Gulf authorities.
In depth: ‘To erect structures, even if they’re temporary, is a red rag to a bull’
The al-Haram al-Sharif site in Jerusalem’s old city, known to Jews as the Temple Mount, is one of the most contentious places on earth. It’s governed by a fragile agreement that gives Muslims exclusive rights to pray and worship there, while Jews pray at the Western Wall below. But Israel’s messianic right, which has gained a powerful foothold in Netanyahu’s coalition government, is fixated on the site as a symbol of its political project. Their vision of building a new Jewish temple on one of Islam’s holiest sites – once a fringe idea – has become increasingly widespread.
Since 2023, Jewish religious extremists have made numerous visits to the 35-acre compound which is home to both al-Aqsa mosque and Dome of the Rock, the holiest sites for Muslims in Jerusalem and one of holiest sites for Muslims in the world. “At first, you had groups of perhaps 20 Jews, mostly settlers, who were escorted by the police to the far wall of the compound to pray discreetly,” Julian tells me. “If you were just a casual visitor, you wouldn’t necessarily see them”. Over the last two years, however, the groups have grown bigger and more audacious. On 23 July, they sang the national anthem, and prayed and performed rituals in the centre of the compound, while Israeli police – who report to Ben-Gvir, who was in attendance – set up tents to provide shade to the worshippers.
“To erect structures, even if they’re temporary, is a red rag to a bull,” Julian says. “The longstanding fear is that Israelis would knock down the Dome of the Rock or the mosque, or rebuild a [Jewish] temple on the site. And these tents were part of a gradual attempt to push the boundaries.” Eight Arab nations swiftly issued a joint statement condemning “mass incursions by settlers led by extremist Israeli ministers”. Last Wednesday, the Jordanian authorities, who administer the site, held an emergency meeting of Arab and Islamic nations to discuss these risks, and afterwards, the Jordanian authorities condemned Israeli violations and warned that they constituted a “blatant provocation” to Muslims worldwide.
“All they can do is issue strong statements, saying, ‘don’t do this’,” says Julian. The Waqf, the Jordanian-appointed foundation that manages the site, is “defenceless”, he explains. In the run-up to Ramadan this year, Waqf sources told the Guardian that five of its staff had been detained by the Shin Bet, Israel’s counterintelligence service. Meanwhile, Israeli police have begun actively recruiting extremist activists to serve in the Temple Mount Unit, the force responsible for policing the compound. According to Haaretz, the deputy commander of the police’s Temple Mount Unit published a callout to officers on social media and in WhatsApp groups associated with West Bank settlers. “Anyone who wants to take part in implementing sovereignty is welcome to contact me,” he wrote.
Why is the site so significant?
The site’s history is constantly enlisted in attempts to justify the present. Muslims know the raised compound in the south-east of Jerusalem as al-Haram al-Sharif (the Noble Sanctuary), or simply al-Aqsa, after the mosque located at its southern edge. Next to the mosque, at the centre of the compound, is the Dome of the Rock, one of the oldest surviving Islamic places of worship. It’s on this site the prophet Muhammad is said to have ascended to heaven.
At the base of the compound is the Western Wall, a section of retaining wall that survived the destruction of the second Jewish temple in 70CE. The Temple Mount is also the holiest site in Judaism, the site of two temples which were built and then destroyed by invaders in ancient times.
Access to the site has been delicately managed for centuries. After the six-day war in 1967, when Israel captured East Jerusalem from Jordan, the Israeli government agreed that Jordan would continue to be the site’s custodian. Since then, the “status quo”, as it is known, has sought to prevent violent conflict by circumscribing the rights of Muslims and Jews to access the compound. While Jews are permitted to visit the site at specific times, they cannot pray there. Many Jews opt not to visit the site, out of fear of treading on holy ground while ritually impure.
“The status quo represented a historic compromise. Jews got the Western Wall. Muslims got Haram al-Sharif,” Julian says. “But the site has always been a detonator, sitting right there in the centre of the old city, with strong religious beliefs crammed together in a small area.”
How has this erupted in the past?
It’s not uncommon in the region for holy sites to be carefully managed with intricate arrangements. Elsewhere in the Old City, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre is divided up between six Christian denominations, with its keys held by two Muslim families. At the Cave of the Patriarchs in the occupied city of Hebron, a mosque and synagogue share one building.
Past Israeli moves to challenge the status quo at al-Haram al-Sharif have been incendiary, sparking deadly violence. In 2000, then Israeli opposition leader and future prime minister Ariel Sharon made a visit to the site in an attempt to demonstrate Israeli sovereignty, sparking a chain of events that helped ignite the second intifada. More recently, Hamas gave the name “al-Aqsa flood” to its attack on Israel in October 2023 that killed 1,200 Israelis and triggered the war on Gaza, claiming it was provoked by Israeli violations at the Jerusalem mosque.

title: Inside stablecoin firm BVNK’s journey to a $1.8B acquisition by Mastercard
full_text:
Inside stablecoin firm BVNK’s journey to a $1.8B acquisition by Mastercard
Early BVNK investor Concentric shares a fascinating inside view on the stablecoin startup’s journey and the eventual Mastercard deal.
- Mastercard recently closed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK for $1.8 billion.
- The deal followed intense competition from Coinbase and Visa, with BVNK ultimately favoring Mastercard over a reportedly higher Coinbase offer because of better cultural fit and strategic alignment.
- The acquisition underscores how major payments players, including Stripe, Visa, Mastercard and Coinbase, are racing to secure positions in the roughly $300 billion stablecoin market..
Long before big-ticket crypto deals and billion-dollar acquisitions make headlines, there’s a long and hard-fought journey, often culminating in a secretive contest where jockeying suitors bid, bluff or walk, until eventually the best match makes it down the aisle. Mastercard’s recent $1.8 billion acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK was no exception.
It’s a process that takes place out of view, under iron-clad non-disclosure agreements, but venture capital firm Concentric — an early investor in BVNK — gave CoinDesk a rare peek behind the curtain, beginning with the startup’s rise and ending with the completion of the deal earlier this week.
The venture capital business is a numbers game. In the case of BVNK, Concentric’s bet paid off: the VC firm backed the stablecoin startup in 2019 at a valuation of just $4 million. Founding partner of Concentric, Kjartan Rist, recalled being introduced to BVNK in 2018.
“They came to us highly recommended by an alumni CEO that we had already backed,” Rist told CoinDesk in an interview. “So, there was a lot of trust there, and this CEO said, ‘You got to meet these guys’. They were serial entrepreneurs coming out of South Africa. They’d never built businesses outside of South Africa, but they were hungry. They were relentless.”
Despite enjoying a sturdy exit, Rist said he feels mixed emotions toward the Mastercard acquisition, having been part of the whole BVNK journey. “It’s actually sad to sign the papers, almost like sending your son off to boarding school,” he said.
Chris Harmse, co-founder and chief business officer at BVNK echoed this: “It's been an incredible journey,” he said in an email. “Concentric has been a valued partner throughout that journey.”
Stablecoins, one of the busiest areas of crypto, have become a focal point for the large card networks and payments players. The total stablecoin market cap is about $300 billion, according to CoinGecko data.
The proverbial cat was set loose among the pigeons when Stripe acquired stablecoin infrastructure firm Bridge in late 2024 for $1.1 billion. This probably put pressure on the likes of Visa and Mastercard to start kicking the tires of other stablecoin shops so as not to be outflanked by Stripe’s aggressive approach.
Mastercard has the deepest respect for Stripe, Rist of Concentric said. “I think that's another way of saying that they're looking over their shoulder. So they are aware of the competitive threat that is coming from Stripe because of the way they execute, the simplicity in their offering and the lack of legacy they have,” he said.
During the cut and thrust of the deal formation, U.S.-listed crypto exchange Coinbase was reported to have had the upper hand at one point, potentially offering as much as $2.5 billion for BVNK. But something changed, which was to do with chemistry, according to Rist.
“The founders, when choosing a partner or choosing someone to buy them, emphasize a lot on the culture and the chemistry,” Rist said. “And the chemistry with Coinbase — although they probably put a bigger number on the table — it didn't work.”
This came down to the fact that Coinbase is an exchange, while Mastercard is a financial services company, Rist added.
“Mastercard was part of the first discussions and BVNK were quite clear when they got into discussions with Mastercard that there was a meeting of minds,” Rist said. “But they decided to try it out with Coinbase. Mastercard stood outside on the porch waiting for them when that didn't work out. So it's been a painless process, to be honest.”
But it wasn’t just Coinbase who muscled in, Rist said. Visa also took a shine to BVNK.
“All the usual suspects were involved, and Visa had an advantage because they were an investor. They made some money out of BVNK…and they actually had an observer position on the board,” Rist said.
In the end, however, Rist said Visa decided not to pursue a potential acquisition. “I think they are adopting a slightly different strategy when it comes to to stablecoins. Rather than owning an operator, they will partner with multiple operators and partner also with Stripe, etcetera,” he said.
CoinDesk recently broke the news that all four firms — Stripe, Visa, Mastercard and Coinbase — were involved in backing a new stablecoin platform, which has since gone live. This only underlines the fact that stablecoins continue to be an area of importance for TradFi institutions despite an ongoing bear market in the crypto industry more broadly.
Looking at specific use cases keeping BVNK busy, Rist pointed to various treasury functions that are streamlined by the use of stablecoins.
“One large payments company working with BVNK rolls its treasury every 24 hours, and now they're using stablecoins to roll it,” he said.
Another benefit comes from the way BVNK and others are servicing companies that have a huge distributed workforce with a number of these workers or freelancers in countries that have very high levels of inflation.
“These firms are using dollar-nominated stablecoins so workers can choose to keep them in their wallets and don’t have to receive pesos or naira, for example,” Rist said.
After backing a winner in the form of BVNK, Concentric is looking for its next stablecoin company to invest in.
“There are hundreds of companies out there now claiming to be the next [big] stablecoin company. In my opinion, only about 10% of these guys are full stack, institutionally verified, and can actually become a winner of some sort,” Rist said. “The other 90% of them are just a front end and some APIs, so it’s our job to figure out who the real guys are.”

title: Robinhood brings crypto trading to UK in AI-powered all-in-one app

The trading firm is also introducing “Robinhood Cortex Digests for Crypto,” a generative AI-powered widget that analyses breaking news and other data.

Robinhood (HOOD) is introducing zero-fee crypto trading in the U.K. alongside stocks and shares ISAs, equities, options and futures, the company said on Monday.
The all-in-one Robinhood app will bring U.K. customers access to over 50 cryptos including Bitcoin

The product also expands Robinhood’s growing crypto ecosystem for UK customers. As such, UK developers can build on the highly popular Robinhood Chain, a layer 2 blockchain built on the Arbitrum platform.
“A new wave of UK investors sees digital assets as an important part of a diversified portfolio,” said Jordan Sinclair, President of Robinhood U.K. “We’re taking another major step toward becoming the all-in-one investment platform for the UK.”

full_text:
BTC above $65,000 even as the Senate punts the CLARITY Act to the fall
Bitcoin held near $65,200 on Monday, up 3.7% on the week, per CoinDesk data. The move caps a recovery from an early-August low near $62,000, and the whole top of the market came with it. Ether traded near $1,925 and BNB, Solana and TRON all posted weekly gains.
The strength held despite the Senate failing to pass the CLARITY Act before leaving for its August recess on Friday, mustering 51 of the 60 votes needed and pushing any action to September 14 at the earliest.
That the market rose anyway backs what strategists argued last week, that the delay was already priced, so the failure landed as confirmation rather than a fresh blow.
The bid is coming from flows, not headlines.
Spot ETFs have strung together consecutive days of inflows, and a softer dollar since the weak US jobs report has loosened the backdrop that pinned bitcoin through the summer.
Michael Saylor added to the mood over the weekend, posting Strategy's bitcoin-buy chart with the caption "Doing business," days after the firm disclosed selling about 1,638 BTC to fund buybacks, which markets read as a tease of another purchase.

title: This bitcoin miner rejected BIP-110 despite mining through a pool that supported it
full_text:
This bitcoin miner rejected BIP-110 despite mining through a pool that supported it
Ocean, a bitcoin mining pool, had been backing BIP-110 by default. Simple Mining, a company that runs mining machines through Ocean, used software from the pool that lets individual miners choose for themselves and went the other way.
- A miner using the Ocean pool’s DATUM protocol declined to signal support for the controversial BIP-110 fork and instead mined block 961,634 on bitcoin’s main chain.
- Simple Mining’s decision underscored that BIP-110 had only about 2.6% of hashrate support, far short of the 55% threshold it sought to restrict non-financial data in transactions for a year.
- After BIP-110 nodes began rejecting non-signaling blocks at height 961,632, the forked chain produced just two blocks before stalling, while the main bitcoin chain advanced more than 200 blocks ahead.
A bitcoin miner chose not to back BIP-110 on Sunday, using a tool from its own mining pool that let it decide what went into the block rather than leaving that to the pool.
Simple Mining said it produced block 961,634 on the main chain, two blocks past the point where BIP-110 supporters broke away.
"Hashrate is a vote you cannot fake, and we decided the proposal wasn't worth following," Simple Mining wrote on X.
We mined block 961,634 using Ocean's DATUM protocol.
The block didn't signal support for BIP-110. 
Support peaked at 2.6% while the proposal needed 55%.
Hashrate is a vote you cannot fake, and we decided the proposal wasn't worth following.
Ocean's DATUM protocol gave us the… https://t.co/YVUeHr2oJ4 pic.twitter.com/wYYq20dsam
The choice is notable because Ocean, the pool it mines with, had switched miners to signal for BIP-110 by default in July and accounted for nearly all of the proposal's small amount of mining support before the split.
BIP-110, short for Bitcoin Improvement Proposal-110, is a move to stop people storing pictures, text and other non-financial data inside bitcoin transactions for a year.
Simple Mining could go the other way because it was using DATUM, an Ocean protocol that gives individual miners control over the blocks they produce.
Mining pools normally combine computing power from many operators so they can find blocks more regularly and share the rewards. The pool usually decides which transactions go into those blocks and what software signals they carry.
DATUM moves that decision back to the individual miner. An operator can build its own block using its own bitcoin software while still contributing computing power to Ocean and sharing in the pool's payouts.
Simple Mining used that control to leave the BIP-110 signal out of block 961,634.
"We chose not to signal and the chain extended on our block," the company said.
That also explains why Ocean has appeared on both sides of the weekend split.
A miner using Ocean produced the first block accepted by the BIP-110 branch on Saturday, according to fork tracker Mempool. Simple Mining then used the same pool and made the opposite choice, producing a block for the dominant bitcoin chain.
Computers running BIP-110 software began rejecting blocks that did not carry its signal at block 961,632, after miner support peaked at about 2.6%, far below the 55% the proposal needed.
The minority branch has struggled since. It produced blocks 961,632 and 961,633 before stalling, while bitcoin kept producing blocks roughly every ten minutes.
By Monday a live monitor showed the main chain at 961,725, putting the BIP-110 branch more than 200 blocks behind.

full_text:
UK regulators to prepare tokenized gold framework: Report
The UK’s FCA is reportedly preparing a regulatory framework for tokenized gold and how these products may be used as collateral assets in wholesale markets.
The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has reportedly held talks with banks and other industry participants over potential rules for tokenized gold.
The FCA has also sought feedback on the use of tokenized gold as collateral in wholesale markets, people familiar with the matter told the Financial Times.
The regulator is reportedly preparing to outline plans for new regulatory standards for tokenized gold. Cointelegraph has approached the FCA for comment on the matter.
London is the world’s largest over-the-counter gold trading hub, accounting for about 70% of global notional gold trading volume, according to the World Gold Council.
The talks come amid a broader UK push to expand tokenized financial markets. A government-backed industry task force said in July that tokenization could add as much as 33 billion British pounds ($44 billion) to the UK’s annual economic output by 2035.
The roadmap also calls for the UK’s first tokenized government bond by early 2027 and seeks to make tokenized securities usable for trading, settlement and as collateral.

title: North Korea’s Kimsuky integrates AI into cyberattacks targeting crypto and finance
summary: Kimsuky uses generative AI to produce phishing documents themed around digital assets, investment strategies, and fintech services.
full_text:
North Korea's Kimsuky integrates AI into cyberattacks targeting crypto and finance
Quick Take
- North Korea’s state-backed hacking group, Kimsuky, is actively incorporating AI tools to enhance its cyberattacks, according to Genians.
- Evidence shows that Kimsuky continues to use generative AI to produce phishing documents themed around digital assets, investment strategies, and fintech services.
We'd love your feedback.
North Korean hacker group Kimsuky is using local AI systems to target cryptocurrency and financial firms with sophisticated cyberattacks, according to a report released Monday by Genians.
The South Korean cybersecurity firm found evidence that the group built and operated three local large language model (LLM) environments using Ollama, GPT4All, and Msty.
These tools allow offline operation and support retrieval-augmented generation, enabling hackers to make queries without sending data to external cloud services.
The group has also collected libraries and frameworks to embed language models into custom software, along with the AI coding assistant Cursor and speech-to-text tools. Genians said this activity focused on integrating existing open-source AI models into malware development, data analysis, and attack automation.
"This provides concrete evidence that the Kimsuky-affiliated threat actor is moving beyond one-off experimentation with AI and is continuously preparing to integrate the technology into actual attack capabilities," Genians noted.
Nonetheless, the research firm stated that Kimsuky appears to remain focused on the integration of existing AI technologies rather than creating entirely new AI models from scratch.
Attack on crypto
At the same time, Genians said it found evidence that Kimsuky continues to use generative AI to produce polished phishing documents themed around digital assets, investment strategies, and fintech services.
Some documents closely imitated materials from a Korean AI-powered investment platform, featuring natural language, consistent, and professional formatting, and design elements typical of AI-generated content.
North Korean hackers stole $2.02 billion worth of cryptocurrency last year, including the $1.5 billion hack of Bybit crypto exchange, according to Chainalysis. The attack methods span from simple phishing emails to embedding IT workers inside crypto services to target sensitive internal data.
Hackers are becoming ever more sophisticated with the advent of AI — NEAR Protocol Co-founder Illia Polosukhin said that AI is supercharging hackers' ability to find software vulnerabilities faster than traditional security can patch them.
The recent $100 million exploit of Coldcard bitcoin hardware wallets is suspected to stem from an obscure vulnerability that AI uncovered.

title: Robinhood brings crypto trading to main UK app through Bitstamp
summary: The launch adds crypto alongside stocks, ISAs, options, and futures in the UK as Robinhood continues to expand its broader crypto ecosystem.
full_text:
Robinhood brings crypto trading to main UK app through Bitstamp
Quick Take
- Robinhood has begun rolling out crypto trading to eligible UK customers through Bitstamp, bringing more than 50 digital assets into its main investing app.
- The launch adds crypto alongside stocks, ISAs, options, and futures in the UK as Robinhood continues to expand its broader crypto ecosystem.
We'd love your feedback.
Robinhood (HOOD) has begun rolling out cryptocurrency trading to eligible customers in the UK, allowing users to buy and sell more than 50 digital assets directly within its main investing app through Bitstamp, the long-serving exchange it acquired for $200 million last year.
The rollout, which starts this week, adds cryptocurrencies to its existing stocks and shares ISAs, equities, options, and futures products in a single application, according to a statement shared with The Block.
Robinhood said the service will launch with zero trading fees, no account maintenance fees, and no custody fees. However, UK customers will pay a 0.1% foreign exchange fee, which rises to 0.3% for certain weekend conversions.
The offering includes assets such as BTC, ETH, XRP, and HYPE. Cryptocurrency trading is provided through Bitstamp UK Ltd, which is registered with the UK Financial Conduct Authority as a crypto asset service provider. Robinhood noted that crypto holdings through Bitstamp UK are not covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme or the Financial Ombudsman Service.
"A new wave of UK investors sees digital assets as an important part of a diversified portfolio," Jordan Sinclair, President of Robinhood UK Ltd and GM of Bitstamp UK Ltd, said. "With today’s launch, we're taking another major step toward becoming the all-in-one investment platform for the UK."
AI-powered crypto analysis
The launch also introduces Robinhood Cortex Digests for Crypto in the UK. The generative AI-powered feature analyzes breaking news, market data, technical indicators, and Robinhood's proprietary insights to explain factors driving price movements in individual crypto assets. It is designed to provide market context to help investors make more informed decisions, according to the firm.
Beyond the new in-app crypto features, Robinhood also highlighted its broader digital asset ecosystem, including Robinhood Chain, its permissionless Arbitrum-based Layer 2 blockchain. Developers can build on the network globally, including in the UK, with Robinhood describing it as being built to "institutional standards."
The company said the network has generated more than $18 billion in decentralized exchange trading volume and surpassed $840 million in total value locked since its July 1 launch.
The UK crypto launch follows the company's recent push to diversify its business beyond trading. Robinhood reported second-quarter crypto transaction revenue of $100 million on July 29, down 38% from a year earlier, while revenue from prediction markets reached $156 million, surpassing crypto for the first time.
Robinhood's total net revenue jumped 32% year-over-year to $1.31 billion, with net income of $573 million representing a 48% increase compared to Q2 2025.
"We delivered record revenues and drove new highs across equity, option, and event contract volumes, as we continue to win market share," Robinhood's Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma said at the time.
During the earnings period, executives also highlighted early traction for Robinhood Chain, with CEO Vlad Tenev saying it had become the fastest Ethereum Virtual Machine-compatible chain to reach 100 million transactions.

title: 澳洲 96 臺比特幣 ATM 全數停機！Cryptolink 遭 AUSTRAC 暫停 3 個月
summary:
澳洲金融情報與洗錢調查局（AUSTRAC）以「連基本申報都做不好」為由，暫停加密貨幣 ATM 營運商 Cryp […]

〈澳洲 96 臺比特幣 ATM 全數停機！Cryptolink 遭 AUSTRAC 暫停 3 個月〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
澳洲金融情報與洗錢調查局（AUSTRAC）以「連基本申報都做不好」為由，暫停加密貨幣 ATM 營運商 Cryptolink 的虛擬資產服務商（VASP）註冊資格 3 個月。旗下 96 臺 ATM 在雪梨、墨爾本、布里斯班等主要城市全部離線，這已經是該公司在 2025 年 10 月因遲報交易遭罰後，一年內第二次被重擊。
（前情提要：澳洲強化加密貨幣 ATM 監管：現金交易上限 5000 澳元、KYC 與監控雙重升級）
（背景補充：加拿大擬立法禁加密 ATM：4,000 臺機器、G7 首例，FINTRAC 資料定調政策邏輯）
澳大利亞金融情報與洗錢調查局（AUSTRAC）週一宣布，對加密貨幣 ATM 營運商 Cryptolink 下達停業處分：暫停其虛擬資產服務商（VASP）註冊資格3 個月，旗下96 臺比特幣 ATM即日起全數離線。
連基本申報都做不好，AUSTRAC 不再通融
AUSTRAC 總裁 Brendan Thomas 在官方宣告中指出，Cryptolink 未能滿足「基本申報要求」，特別是門檻交易報告（Threshold Transaction Reports，TTRs）長期未如實提交，且在公司多次收到 AUSTRAC 的資訊請求後沒有回應。
門檻交易報告是反洗錢合規的核心機制之一：當單筆或累計交易超過法定門檻（澳洲為 10,000 澳元或等值外幣）時，VASP 必須在 10 個工作日內向 AUSTRAC 申報。Thomas 表示：
「作為我們持續關注數位貨幣作為洗錢風險的一部分，AUSTRAC 對 Cryptolink 管理其加密 ATM 高風險交易的能力，有持續的疑慮。」
這不是第一次：2025 年已罰過、簽過承諾書
Cryptolink 這次遭停權，其實已經是第二次處分。就在不到一年前的2025 年 10 月，AUSTRAC 的加密貨幣專責小組（Cryptocurrency Taskforce）就對其展開調查，查出包括遲報交易與風險評估缺失等違規行為。
當時 AUSTRAC 對 Cryptolink 下了兩記重拳：
- 強制承諾協議（enforceable undertaking）：Cryptolink 必須承諾改善合規流程
- 行政罰鍰：開罰 56,340 澳元（約 3.7 萬美元），Cryptolink 已繳款
Cryptolink 當時也在官方宣告中承認違規，並承諾升級內部合規機制。但從 AUSTRAC 這次「直接停業」的處分來看，整改顯然沒有達標。
96 臺 ATM 全數離線，雪梨、墨爾本受影響最大
根據 AUSTRAC 公告，Cryptolink 目前在全澳洲營運96 臺加密貨幣 ATM，主要分布在三大都市區：
- 雪梨（Sydney）
- 墨爾本（Melbourne）
- 布里斯班（Brisbane）
這些 ATM 讓顧客可以用現金直接購買比特幣，無需銀行帳戶或 KYC 審核，這正是監管機構最擔心的部分。
澳洲：亞太最多加密 ATM，也是打擊最狠的國家之一
根據 CoinATMRadar 的資料，澳洲擁有亞太地區最多的加密貨幣 ATM，這讓該國成為洗錢與詐欺風險的重點監管物件。
AUSTRAC 自2024 年底起就持續針對加密 ATM 的犯罪用途展開打壓，包括：
- 2025 年中推出更嚴格現金交易上限（5,000 澳元）
- 要求所有 ATM 營運商強制 KYC 與即時監控
- 針對未合規業者直接停權，不再以罰鍰了事
Cryptolink 這次成為第一個被直接停業 3 個月的加密 ATM 營運商，顯示澳洲監管正從「罰款教育」轉向「實質限制營業」。
市場觀察：加密 ATM 的生存空間正在收縮
Cryptolink 的處分，放在全球加密 ATM 監管趨勢來看，是一記強烈的訊號。
加密 ATM 因為「現金→加密貨幣」的匿名性，長期被詐騙集團、洗錢者、逃稅者利用。澳洲 AUSTRAC、美國 FinCEN、加拿大 FINTRAC 三大情報單位在過去一年都顯著提高了對 VASP 的監管強度。
Cryptolink 的問題不是「沒有合規」，而是「連基本合規都做不好」，遲報交易、不回應監管機構的資料請求、風險評估缺失，這些都是最低階的合規瑕疵。一個在「入門級要求」就掛點的業者，被直接停業並不意外。
後續觀察：
- 3 個月後 Cryptolink 能否復業？AUSTRAC 要求整改，能否透過審查還要看
- 其他澳洲 ATM 營運商是否被連坐調查？AUSTRAC 的 Cryptocurrency Taskforce 已證明有系統性掃蕩能力
- 加密 ATM 模式在亞太區的長期前景：當 KYC 與申報成為剛性成本，低毛利 ATM 業務能否存活
對想靠現金買賣比特幣的澳洲使用者來說，接下來的三個月，街頭那臺熟悉的機器恐怕暫時不亮了。

title: 英國正著手製定代幣化黃金監管框架，FCA 與大型銀行已展開討論
summary:
英國金融行為監管局（FCA）正在與大型銀行討論「代幣化黃金」的監管框架，作為推動金融市場數位化、維持倫敦全球黃 […]

〈英國正著手製定代幣化黃金監管框架，FCA 與大型銀行已展開討論〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
英國金融行為監管局（FCA）正在與大型銀行討論「代幣化黃金」的監管框架，作為推動金融市場數位化、維持倫敦全球黃金交易中心地位的一環。未來數月，監管部門預計將公布相關監管標準制定計畫。
（前情提要：英國金管局：年底推出「代幣化基金」，採區塊鏈分散式帳本技術！）
（背景補充：英國 FCA 加密監管框架拍板！2027 年 2 月授權大限，牌照申請 9 月起跑）
英國金融行為監管局（FCA）正著手製定「代幣化黃金」的監管框架，這是英國推動金融市場數位化、鞏固倫敦作為全球黃金交易中心地位的計畫之一。FCA 已就代幣化黃金的監管方式與業界機構展開討論，其中包括多家大型銀行，未來數月內監管部門預計將公布相關監管標準的制定計畫。
英國以「代幣化基礎設施」拉高金融壁壘
這並非英國首次針對數位資產和代幣化資產推出監管框架。2025 年，英國已將穩定幣納入正式監管體系，並由 FCA 與英國央行共同制定系統級穩定幣的監管標準。2026 年 5 月，FCA 與英國央行進一步發布「代幣化在英國批發市場的共享願景」，明確支援以代幣化技術提升清算與結算效率。
在這樣的脈絡下，「代幣化黃金」框架的推出可視為英國監管機構將代幣化從穩定幣、批發市場進一步延伸到「實體資產代幣化（RWA）」的延續動作。黃金作為全球最大的避險資產，其代幣化市場早已由 Pax Gold（PAXG）、Tether Gold（XAUt）等加密原生專案主導；英國此次試圖建立監管框架，等於是把「合規入口」握在自己手裡，讓傳統金融機構也能以合規方式參與這個市場。
倫敦想保住黃金交易中心，必須接受鏈上黃金
倫敦是全球最大的黃金交易中心，每日黃金交易量約佔全球 40% 以上。但近年來，新興市場與數位資產的崛起，使得黃金交易正逐漸向鏈上平台延伸。若英國不主動建立代幣化黃金監管框架，其他司法管轄區如瑞士、新加坡可能搶先定義標準，倫敦的優勢將受到威脅。
與業界包括大型銀行的討論，暗示英國希望將代幣化黃金納入現有金融體系，而非另建一個「加密黃金」生態。這意味著未來的代幣化黃金產品，很可能需要符合 FCA 的客戶資金保護、儲備審計、反洗錢（AML）等要求，與英國現有的穩定幣監管邏輯相似。
對加密市場的意義：合規 RWA 的下一波
代幣化黃金的監管框架若順利落地，將為「實體資產代幣化（RWA）」再添一塊合規拼圖。對加密市場而言，這代表傳統金融機構進軍 RWA 的門檻更清晰，也意味著鏈上黃金產品的流動性與機構採用率有機會提升。
不過，短期內這仍停留在監管討論階段。FCA 尚未公布具體時間表、合規要求，或是否會與現有代幣化黃金專案（如 PAXG）直接對接。市場需觀察未來數月的官方公告。

title: 韓國金管局啟動升級，10 月起虛擬資產語音詐騙損失納入賠償範圍
summary:
韓國 FSS 啟動賠償系統改革，10 月起虛擬資產詐騙損失納入退賠範圍，賠償計算從固定金額改為比例制。 （前情 […]

〈韓國金管局啟動升級，10 月起虛擬資產語音詐騙損失納入賠償範圍〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
韓國 FSS 啟動賠償系統改革，10 月起虛擬資產詐騙損失納入退賠範圍，賠償計算從固定金額改為比例制。
（前情提要：韓國五大交易所 6 年爆 57 起事故、賠 70 億韓元）
（背景補充：韓國加密新規 7 月上路：最高處無期徒刑、強制保險）
韓國金融監督院（FSS）於 8 月 6 日正式啟動「金融詐騙損失賠償系統改善計畫」，將現行以韓元為中心的賠償計算方式全面改革，為今年 10 月起把虛擬資產損失納入賠償範圍做準備。
根據 SBS 新聞網報導，FSS 這次改革針對的是目前賠償系統無法處理加密資產價差的問題。現行制度主要根據以韓元計價的損失來計算賠償金額，但虛擬資產價格波動劇烈，固定幣值計算方式經常低估實際損失。
賠償計算從「固定金額」改為「比例制」
改革完成後的新系統將引入三項重要改變：
- 賠償比例制：不再以固定韓元金額計算，改用賠償比例，根據受害者的損失佔比來決定退還金額
- 資產型別與數量納入考量：不同虛擬資產（比特幣、以太坊、穩定幣等）的波動特性將分別計入賠償演算法
- 暫停支付時即計算匯率：民眾被詐騙時凍結帳戶，虛擬資產會按凍結當時的韓元兌換價值計算，避免後續價格波動影響
這意味著，未來受害者被詐騙轉走 1 枚比特幣，賠償金額不再以「報案時點」的 BTC 價格為基準，而是以帳戶暫停那一刻的即時匯率鎖定，確保賠償更精準。
語音詐騙成韓國加密損失主因
根據 SBS 的調查，語音詐騙（Whispering / 詐騙通話）已成為韓國虛擬資產損失的主要來源。詐騙集團透過 AI 語音克隆或假裝成交易所客服，誘導民眾將加密貨幣轉入假錢包。
FSS 在 8 月 6 日啟動改革後，預計於 10 月前完成系統升級。屆時，虛擬資產持有者若因詐騙造成損失，可直接透過 FSS 的線上賠償平台申請退還，無需先走訴訟程序。
同日平行進展：虛擬資產稅收延後三年
韓國加密監管動態在同日也出現另一筆。8 月 10 日，韓國國民力量黨議員鄭成國提出法案，擬將虛擬資產收入稅收從原定的 2027 年 1 月延後至2030 年 1 月，為期三年。這顯示韓國在擴大賠償覆蓋範圍的同時，也同步調整稅收政策以減輕投資者負擔。
韓國目前是亞洲加密監管最積極的市場之一。早在 2026 年 6 月，FSS 就公布五大交易所 6 年內爆發 57 起事故的資料，推動監管立法要求業者無條件賠償使用者。

title: 馬斯克狂飆10GW算力：SpaceX建5000億，微軟當大買家
summary:
SemiAnalysis 分析指出，馬斯克計劃 2027 年新增 6-8GW 算力，資本開支高達 3000-5 […]

〈馬斯克狂飆10GW算力：SpaceX建5000億，微軟當大買家〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
SemiAnalysis 分析指出，馬斯克計劃 2027 年新增 6-8GW 算力，資本開支高達 3000-5000 億美元，與 AWS、谷歌相當。每 GW 年營收可超 1000 億美元，微軟以每 GW 500 億美元簽約 3GW，有望成為最大客戶。
（前情提要：SpaceX 獨家鎖定輝達 AI 架構，太空資料中心 Starmind 計劃明年啟動）
（背景補充：Anthropic 完成 650 億美元 H 輪融資，估值 9,650 億美元超越 OpenAI）
SemiAnalysis 最新深度報告揭露，馬斯克正把 SpaceX 打造成全球最大的 AI 算力供應商——2027 年單年新增 6-8GW，資本開支直逼 AWS 與谷歌。這不是空談：從推理收益、微軟需求到建設速度，三個維度都指向同一個結論——算力軍備競賽已進入吉瓦級時代，而 SpaceX 可能是唯一能兌現承諾的玩家。
馬斯克在 SpaceX 首次財報電話會上再次震撼業界，宣布了他的千兆瓦級雄心：他「保守地」計劃在 2027 年單年新增 6–8GW 算力，實際數字可能超過 10GW。按每 GW 投入 500 億美元計算，這相當於 2027 年投入 3000–5000 億美元資本開支，與我們預期 AWS 和谷歌的投入相當——對於一家盈利能力遠不如競爭對手的公司來說，這個數字難以想像。
正如我們在 Meta 算力深度分析中解釋的，大規模 + 短交付週期的算力是極其稀有的組合，定價有巨大超額定價——高達每 GW 每年 500 億美元。但 AI 實驗室能承受這個價格，並且活得很好。
我們的 Tokenomics 模型和推理模擬器顯示，在實際效能水平下（例如每 GPU 的 tokens/秒），OpenAI 和 Anthropic 在 GB300 叢集上銷售 API 推理服務，都能產生每 GW 每年超過 1000 億美元的營收。這遠高於按當前新雲服務商價格租用 GB300 叢集一年的成本。
對前沿模型公司來說，提供推理 token 服務的利潤高得亮眼。
我們假設每 GW 每年成本約 120 億美元，採用保守的租賃價格每 GPU 小時 3 美元，並使用我們的推理模擬器基於前沿模型架構和我們的代理程式設計基準 AgentX（InferenceX 的一部分，基於真實生產程式設計軌跡構建）進行 token 產出估算。我們將該 token 產出率按輸入、快取讀取、快取寫入和輸出 token 成本以及真實工作負載比例混合計算，得出最終估值超過每 GW 每年 1000 億美元。
微軟10GW大覺醒：每MW年賺1億美元的算力生意
我們的推理模擬器是從底層開始構建的，基於對現代 AI 加速器工作原理的基礎理解。我們為前沿模型在推理過程中的工作方式構建了效能上限和實際效能模型，為每個操作計時並輸出真實軌跡。這是在實際矽片上執行實際工作負載的端到端模擬。我們已在各種加速器和工作負載上驗證了模擬器的準確性，並持續改進其基於設計規格預測未來加速器效能的能力。
除了 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，世界上實際上還有第三家公司能實現每 GW 這樣的經濟效益：微軟。由於完全享有 OpenAI 模型訪問權，他們可以產生完全相同的每 MW 營收和利潤率，同時無需支付任何訓練成本。納德拉與 OpenAI 的談判非常成功：2026 年 4 月重新修訂的協議取消了舊的 20% 營收分成。簡而言之，微軟有巨大動力盡可能快地採購儘可能多的 MW 算力。雖然他們目前大部分資料中心容量以每 MW 每年 1400 萬美元的價格給 OpenAI 使用，但他們有機會改善這個組合。潛在影響是微軟 Azure 營收增長率從約 42% 加速到明年超過 100%。這是百年一遇的機會，而 SpaceX 在服務這一需求上佔據極佳位置。
雖然微軟以每 GW 每年 500 億美元與 SpaceX 簽約 3GW 聽起來激進，但我們認為這是可能的，原因有二：
- 微軟已在為大規模資料中心擴張做準備。如下文所述，他們今年迄今已簽署 10GW 合同，總合同價值超過 3000 億美元（不含 GPU 成本）。我們預計還會籤更多。需要說明的是：這些合同貢獻的是 2027 年底和 2028 年的容量，近期仍有缺口需要填補。
- 有 90 天取消政策，類似 SpaceX 與 Anthropic 和谷歌的協議，資產負債表零風險。考慮到營收機會，Amy Hood 很容易批准這個方案。
推理利潤驚人：每GW年營收破千億美元
對 SpaceX 來說，下一個自然的問題是融資。在沒有頂級超大規模雲服務商的資產負債表支撐下，埃隆如何支付如此高的資本開支？我們預計以下兩種方式的組合：
- 輝達的支援，以供應商融資形式降低前期現金成本。這可能就是埃隆在財報電話會上宣布獨家使用輝達的原因！正如我們的加速器模型反覆解釋的，xAI/SpaceX 積極評估過 TPU 和 AMD 等替代方案——因此財務考量可能促使他們放棄這些選項，專注於輝達。
- 由產業最高定價支撐的經營現金流融資，依靠最快的交付週期：SpaceX 將繼續以 3–5 個月的交付週期銷售大規模算力——這是無人能及的供給——並相應定價為每 MW 每年 3000–5000 萬美元。這在不到一年內就能收回資本開支。我們在 Meta 算力文章中深入探討了這一點。
這意味著 SpaceX 有望在 2027 年底實現 3000 億美元 ARR。這隻假設他們 2027 年新增算力的 50% 實現商業化，其餘留給 Grok 和 Cursor 團隊用於訓練（未建模推理營收）。
現在讓我們深入分析。我們從微軟開始，微軟終於亮眼地甦醒了：去年的暫停已經逆轉，今年迄今已簽署 10GW 的有約束力合同。我們將簡要討論如何實現每 MW 每年 1 億美元推理營收的經濟模型。然後轉向 SpaceX，分析他們的資料中心擴張以及 2027 年底實現 10GW+ 的可行性。
馬斯克速度：122天建Colossus，5個月再造500MW
2024 年 12 月，我們在資料中心模型中率先指出微軟租賃活動的顯著暫停。今天，這個巨頭醒了。我們的模型逐季度跟蹤租賃活動、新雲服務商簽約、自建施工啟動，以及大型有約束力的 PPA 和 ESA。下圖顯示輸出結果。微軟在所有這些方面簽約超過 10GW，相當於約 3000 億美元的新有約束力承諾。
這次甦醒的一個關鍵原因是他們迫切需要算力來抓住每 MW 年營收 1 億美元的機會。微軟在 2025 年 10 月與 OpenAI 簽署了 2500 億美元協議，我們在 Tokenomics 模型中估計總計約 7GW——這是理解美元到瓦特數學關係細微差別的全球最佳工具。這筆大規模基礎設施即服務交易導致微軟在其他用例上算力高度受限。他們一直無法利用其 OpenAI 模型訪問權來開展 API 業務 Foundry，或用於 Copilot 等應用。
然而，這些服務的利潤率和每 MW 營收是迄今為止最高的。我們在 AI 價值捕獲文章中深入解釋過這一點。
AI 領域的一天感覺像其他產業的一年。模型發布、軟體突破和硬體改進正在將其他產業需要數年的週期壓縮到幾周。就在過去幾個月，代理 AI 跨越了真正的拐點，在軟體和硬體改進大幅降低 token 生成成本的同時，推動 token 價值實現階躍式增長。
為了得出這些利潤率估算，我們必須仔細綜合洩露的財務資料、InferenceX 資料、產業所有最新加速器的微基準測試、開源實驗室的論文、部落格和推文等等。DeepSeek 投資者電話會議洩露（他們說 GPU 回收期為 10 個月）等新資料點證實我們的估算在正確範圍內，但我們首先承認缺乏粒度確實令人不滿。比起公司整體推理毛利率這個單一數字，你真正想知道的是在整個吞吐量 vs 延遲帕累託前沿上，每個（模型，加速器）組合的毛利率。例如，在 Trainium3 上提供 Opus 5 Fast 與在 TPUv7 上提供 Fable 5 的毛利率分別是多少？
我們用推理模擬器回答這個問題，該工具僅向 SemiAnalysis 諮詢客戶提供。
跳過變壓器、搶購渦輪機：SpaceX的建站捷徑
我們的 AI 雲 TCO 模型已經回答了成本方面的問題，但營收方面歷史上是未知的。為瞭解決這個問題，我們編寫了一個模擬框架，在虛擬硬體上模擬真實模型執行，由涵蓋各種加速器和操作型別的調優細粒度效能模型支撐。我們在模擬 XPU 上以所有可能的服務配置執行每個模型，混合真實世界和理想化服務條件。這使我們能夠在對模型架構有充分了解假設的情況下，準確估算軟體、硬體和工作負載的任何組合的效能。
得益於這個模擬器，我們的 Tokenomics 模型現在包含在所有相關晶片上執行 OpenAI/Anthropic 旗艦模型的高層級每 MW 營收數字。工作負載形態顯然是一個巨大因素，我們模擬執行從我們自己使用中收集的超過 100 萬美元價值的代理軌跡，同時滿足從訪問第一方端點觀察到的真實互動性和 TTFT 水平。作為預告，這是我們在 GB200 vs GB300 上提供 Fable 5 的數字：
這就是微軟每 MW 1 億美元的機會。鑑於最近 Codex 需求激增和相應的 OpenAI ARR 加速，我們相信微軟透過提供 OAI 模型服務能夠以類似速率實現算力商業化。
現在，要抓住這個百年一遇的機會，微軟和 AI 實驗室需要資料中心，而且要快、要大。SpaceX 已經兩次證明他們的建設速度比其他人快，但到 2026 年底他們的算力容量「僅」為 2GW。他們真的能在 2027 年這一年內建成 10GW+ 嗎？
在我們的 Meta 算力文章中，我們深入解釋了為什麼埃隆再次證明自己是商業奇才。他理解 AI 實驗室利潤率已大幅提升，並相應地為他的 GPU 叢集引入了「基於價值定價」，而不是更常見的「成本加成」。
為了保持機器運轉，埃隆需要比任何人都更快地建設資料中心。我們相信他能做到。是什麼給了我們這種信心？我們寫過幾次關於埃隆速度的文章，包括 122 天建成 Colossus 1 的 300MW、六個月建成 Colossus 2 的 200MW、決定在邊境對面 1 公里處建設現場發電廠以避免許可審批等等。
融資密碼：輝達供應商貸款+3-5個月回本
此後還有更多速度展示。Southaven 的發電廠已從 2026 年 2 月的 27 臺渦輪機（約 495MW）擴充套件到 2026 年 7 月的 69 臺渦輪機（1.7GW）。
還有「MiniHard」的出現，2026 年 3 月開始垂直建設後，可能在約 5 個月內就達到 450–500MW！這並不意味著埃隆比其他人建得更好。他只是採用了不同的方法。
配電裝置和大功率變壓器已售罄兩年？直接從中國購買電力模組，跳過大功率變壓器，將中壓電力從發電端直接輸送到低壓變壓器——後者的供應要充裕得多。Elon 旗下公司擁有世界上最優秀的電氣工程師——沒人比他們更懂如何權衡速度與效率。全球大多數資料中心營運商都優先考慮效率和質量——這是拿下 15–20 年承諾制超大規模雲服務商合同的唯一途徑。SpaceX 則會專注於完全不同的權衡：速度至上。在算力緊缺、AI token 利潤率極高的時期，一個能在三個月內交付、90 天解約期的 500MW 叢集，是世界上最稀有、最有價值的資產之一。所有常規的「質量」指標都不重要。證據？全球垂直整合程度最高的基礎設施公司 Google，最終還是選擇了與 SpaceX 簽約。
燃氣輪機訂單已排到 5 年後？GE Vernova 的確如此，但還有很多其他選擇——我們的能源模型顯示，有 30 多家燃氣發電裝置製造商已拿到為資料中心服務的大規模訂單。只要你足夠努力尋找，並願意與新供應商合作，就有大量可用產能。渦輪機二級市場的成交量正在激增——例如，原本計劃交付給 Oracle 新墨西哥州站點的所有渦輪機現在都在市場上流通。二級市場價格很高，但 Elon 付得起。
人力是最終制約？那就儘可能並行作業，簡化除錯流程，儘可能多地預裝配。據報道，Colossus 2 高峰期每日用工約 3000 名建築工人，比其他在建的吉瓦級資料中心少約一半。Elon 長期以來一直用低於產業標準的人力完成創舉——看看 Tesla 和 SpaceX 的歷史就知道了。
這足以留出充足時間，在 2027 年前建成多個這樣的外殼。而且這是他第一個真正意義上的綠地專案，下一次很可能做得更好。當然，另一個選擇是改造現有設施。正如我們去年關於 xAI 的深度分析中所述，Colossus 1 和 2 都是透過改造以亮眼的速度建成的。
關於 xAI 的 Colossus 1 已有大量報道。孟菲斯的建設註定寫入歷史：全球最大的 AI 訓練叢集，從零開始僅用 122 天建成。憑藉約 20 萬塊 H100/H200 和約 3 萬塊 GB200 NVL72，它至今仍是最大的完全執行、單一連貫的叢集（Google 除外）。
一年內建成 10+GW 則完全是另一個故事。SpaceX 需要在全國範圍內尋找合適的土地，要易於獲得許可且能接入天然氣。但我們相信，有足夠多的選項支撐大規模擴張。這自然會大量依賴現場燃氣發電——檢視我們的能源深度分析，瞭解它的運作原理及其必要性。
在付費牆之後，我們將討論一些我們推測 Elon 可能選擇的站點。

title: Google 發表會週四登場，Pixel 新品傳聞搶先看
summary: 一年一度 Made by Google 發表會將在台灣時間本週四於美國紐約舉行，其中 Pixel 11 系列手 […]
full_text:
一年一度 Made by Google 發表會將在台灣時間本週四於美國紐約舉行，其中 Pixel 11 系列手機確認同日開放預購，各項銷售方面台灣同步跟進，快速一覽 Pixel 新品有何看點。
Pixel 11 全系列
首先，Pixel 11、Pixel 11 Pro、Pixel 11 Pro XL 這 3 款直立式新機共同核心是，預計搭載全新 Tensor G6 晶片和 Titan M2 安全性輔助處理器，採台積電 2 奈米製程生產，記憶體皆提供 12GB 和 16GB 的選擇，支援 Qi2 無線充電，採用 Android 17 系統。
6.3 吋螢幕的 Pixel 11 將是全系列最輕、尺寸最小的款式，預期後置雙鏡頭包含 4,800 萬像素主鏡頭和 1,300 萬像素超廣角鏡頭，支援最高 30 倍超高解析縮放，配備 4,985mAh 電池。
專業版 Pixel 11 Pro、Pixel 11 Pro XL 分別是 6.3 吋、6.8 吋螢幕，峰值亮度比 Pixel 11 高，預期旗艦級後置三鏡頭包含 5,000 萬像素主鏡頭、4,800 萬像素超廣角鏡頭、4,800 萬像素望遠鏡頭鏡頭（支援 5 倍光學變焦），電池分別配備 4,850mAh、5,115mAh。其中 XL 版本的儲存空間除 256GB、512GB 外，還提供 1TB 可選，而 512GB 和 1TB 直接配備 16GB 記憶體，有線充電規格更提升至 45W 快充。
摺疊手機 Pixel 11 Pro Fold，主螢幕 8 吋、外螢幕 6.4 吋皆支援 120Hz 螢幕更新率。預期後置三鏡頭包含 4,800 萬像素主鏡頭、1,050 萬像素超廣角鏡頭、1,080 萬像素望遠鏡頭（支援 5 倍光學變焦）；而在主螢幕和外螢幕上，各配備一顆 1,000 萬像素前置鏡頭，皆支援臉部辨識解鎖。新機搭載 4,806mAh 電池，並支援 30W 有線快充。
Google 裝置與服務副總裁 Shakil Barkat 先前接受外媒 9to5Google 採訪幾乎證實，Pixel 11 系列價格高於 Pixel 10。以美國建議售價來看，新機售價傳為 Pixel 11 899 美元、Pixel 11 Pro 1,099 美元、Pixel 11 Pro XL 1,299 美元、Pixel 11 Pro Fold 1,899 美元，均漲價 100 美元。考慮到 AI 資料中心需求暴增，導致記憶體供不應求，同時其他零組件成本也上升，新機漲價不令人意外。
值得一提的是，新機帶來新的配色，並傳出機身背面採霧面質感設計。先前傳出 Pixel 11 系列新增「Pixel Glow」功能，可能以「HiLight」為名提供給使用者，官方宣傳視覺已能看到相機系統的 LED 燈。當手機反面朝上擺放時，透過後置鏡頭旁的 LED 燈閃爍可掌握手機動態，但就是一個小設計，具體作用則待 Google 揭曉。
▲ Pixel 11 傳聞新色。（Source：MyMobiles）
Pixel Watch 5 手錶、Pixel Tag 追蹤器
Google 在宣傳文案定位 Pixel Watch 5 為「追蹤你的健康、睡眠及健身」的智慧手錶，預期與去年型號相似。
Pixel Watch 5 預期採用與上一代相同的 Snapdragon Wear W5 Gen 2 晶片處理器，擁有相同的螢幕，提供 41 毫米和 45 毫米 2 種螢幕尺寸。然而 Pixel Watch 5 的記憶體首次從 2GB 升級至 3GB，可能有助於解鎖 Gemini Intelligence 的能力，並期待新功能隨新錶推出。
除此之外，一張名為 Pixel Tag 的新型追蹤器圖片日前流出，這款產品的設計是對應蘋果 AirTag。Google 為 Android 平台開發尋找中心（Find Hub），但還沒有類似 AirTag 防丟用途的產品，或許這次可以期待 Pixel Tag 的推出。
▲ Pixel Watch 5 可望推出 NBA 球星 Stephen Curry 聯名款。（Source：MyMobiles）
Google 去年就曾表示，Pixel 設計將是每 2~3 年改變一次，暗示未來 Pixel 11 變化不大。
從流出資訊可以看出，Pixel 11 規格無顯著外觀變化或規格升級，恐怕也無重大功能突破，但價格卻是有感上漲，這些加起來導致新機銷售可能較為艱難。站在消費者立場，發表後甚至可以評估功能和價格，看看去年上市的 Pixel 10 系列是否仍為值得入手的選項。
Pixel 手機這年來憑藉 Tensor 自研晶片和深度整合的 Gemini 應用，試圖在手機市場震盪中突圍，就看消費者願不願以買單。

title: The team behind Hodgkinson's golden rise and the hunt for a world record
summary: BBC Sport looks at the team behind Great Britain 800m star Keely Hodgkinson's golden rise and pursuit of a world record.
full_text:
The Olympic champion and the world silver medallist over 800m embrace by the side of the track after surviving their latest brutal training session together during an east Manchester downpour.
A short while ago, Keely Hodgkinson lay flat out on the track.
Coach Trevor Painter, aware it may be some time before Hodgkinson can move again, places an opened umbrella beside his star athlete to shield her from the incessant rain, before running for cover.
It requires the assistance of two team-mates to eventually peel her off the ground.
Georgia Hunter Bell, meanwhile, uses the little energy she has left to take herself away to be sick.
Observing it all, Painter jokes he is mostly disappointed that relatively few of their team-mates have suffered the same fate on this occasion, when the cameras are rolling.
This is, after all, what it takes to be part of M11 Track Club, where the emphasis is on fun until the stopwatch starts.
Named after the postcode in which it is based, the near-30 strong international training group continue to create history under the guidance of the meticulous Painter and partner Jenny Meadows, a world medallist who has put herself through all the anguish she now oversees.
There is no doubt in the mind of Hodgkinson, winner of six global medals in as many years as a professional athlete, about the important role of this support system in her monumental achievements.
"I think it's everything," the 24-year-old Hodgkinson tells BBC Sport.
"I probably wouldn't be the person I am without it. We have a very fun approach to training, I love everybody in this group.
"Environment is everything. We have people from all around the world training here. We all get along really well, we're all respective of each other's journey, and we all know that if we want to continue being the best, we've got to train with the best.
"And it works."
The sense of community and camaraderie among individuals from around the globe is instantly evident as the team arrive and gather in a small room to begin their activation work and receive light physiotherapy.
Newest recruit Gaia Sabbatini, who has traded training in Rome to be here, is welcomed with happy birthday wishes and balloons - but there is a prevailing sense of apprehension among the athletes about what lies in store.
The miserable weather is the least of their worries, and it will not be long before the Italian is telling us all that she feels like she is "dying".
Painter might be the only one laughing and joking at that stage, but that is mostly founded in the knowledge that, by the time they are done here, they will each be sufficiently exhausted to know they are another step closer to realising their goals.
This is, after all, part of the deal.
"I'm really passionate about the environment we've created," Painter says.
"There are a lot of friendships, it is like a family. But, when the time comes, you roll your sleeves up.
"There will be people bent over being sick and going to a very dark place during training, but the friendships and the fun that we have make it that little bit easier."
A lactic acid-inducing session comprising 400m intervals in early June signals the start of a specific 800m training block to prepare for the summer's major targets.
That Hodgkinson was able to run a British 800m record in Stockholm just a few days before, having not begun her event-specific work, was cause for significant optimism, albeit she was outshone by Swiss athlete Audrey Werro clocking the fastest time since the world record was set 43 years ago.
Despite the conditions, Painter informs us that Hodgkinson, perhaps motivated by that unexpected defeat, has outperformed all expectations. She has beaten her personal best splits for this session, going faster than times posted in the lead-up to an outstanding indoor season in which she captured world gold and the indoor 800m world record.
The M11 foundations were in place long before Hodgkinson's father suggested the group's now globally recognised title.
Painter, who boasts a background in rugby league and an impressive 47-second 400m time, has overseen Hodgkinson's development since she was 17. Before then, he coached Meadows to international success.
It has taken just two years for Meadows' vision of an official Manchester-based training group to become reality and earn a global reputation.
"I think everyone thought I was quite deluded. I had a vision of this happening, but I didn't quite know how we were going to achieve it," says Meadows.
"At first, when we would hear people from other nations talk about M11, I was almost like, 'oh my gosh, they've said M11'. It's almost like a project that I brought home from school, and people are talking about it.
"Now people know instantly: that's Jenny and Trevor, that's some of the best athletes in the world. You don't have to explain what M11 is. It's pretty incredible."
Reaching that stage was never a given.
The process was undoubtedly accelerated by Hodgkinson's rise to Olympic gold, and further medals at Paris 2024 for team-mates Hunter Bell and Lewis Davey.
The sustained success on the track has allowed Painter and Meadows to expand the scale of their operation, with backing from big-name sponsors helping to add an assistant coach, track-side physiotherapist and dedicated physiologist.
"Back in the day, it was difficult because you're working on a shoestring budget, trying to make things happen," says Painter.
"But, as Keely comes along and does well, you get a little bit of help from here and there.
"Then, as more people come and we have more success, we can go back to the sponsors and they give us a little more. It pays for strength and conditioning support, nutrition support, trackside physiotherapy - all which keep the athletes healthy.
"If they're healthy, they can do their job of running as fast as they can."
- Defiant Hodgkinson says home European title would mean as much as Olympic gold 
  - Published13 hours ago
- Hunter Bell eyes ambitious sweep after Glasgow gold 
  - Published31 July
The public-use SportCity track in the shadows of Manchester City's Premier League stadium, the occasional car park in Wigan, and the famous dirt track ascending 'hell hill' on South Africa training camps are humbling, no-nonsense settings for some of the world's top athletes to be honing their craft.
But they are very much in keeping with the values which Painter and Meadows have instilled in a group that continue to hit spectacular heights.
There are no egos among a carefully hand-picked selection of athletes who push each other on and, when needed, pick each other up.
The knock-on positive impact on athletic performance, in what is typically considered an individual sport, is at the heart of what Painter and Meadows have built - and why they continue to prioritise protecting that ecosystem.
"The team aspect is so powerful. It doesn't matter which athlete it is; if someone's having a bad day, there's always someone to put their arm around you or give you that little motivational comment that helps you back out of your mood," says Painter.
"We celebrate each and everybody's wins - and we suffer each and everyone's losses, pains and injuries.
"People who come into the squad, they look around and they see the Olympic champion on her hands and knees being sick, and the next minute she's getting ice poured over her. It's like, 'oh, right, that's normal, is it?'"
Despite social media evidence to the contrary, Painter pleads he is "not always the culprit" when it comes to the pouring of ice buckets.
As the group's pursuit of global titles and world records has gathered momentum, it has left no shortage of prospective athletes desperate to be invited in.
Painter and Meadows are inundated with applications from eager individuals via social media, email and in person, while sponsors Nike will also suggest athletes for their consideration.

title: How Liverpool are shaping up under Iraola
summary: Four pre-season games is a very small sample, but Andoni Iraola is starting to put his stamp on Liverpool. So how are the Reds shaping up under their new boss?
full_text:
How Liverpool are shaping up under Iraola
- Published
Winning is important - but for many fans, how a team plays in the hunt for wins is almost as significant.
When results don't come, a style that fans enjoy watching often buys a manager more time than a pragmatist might be afforded.
Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot as Liverpool head coach a season after the latter won the Premier League with the Reds.
Many believe the Spanish coach's style is more aligned with the 'heavy metal' style of football Anfield had come to love under Jurgen Klopp.
So how have Liverpool fared in their pre-season games so far under Iraola?
Liverpool have beaten Sunderland and Wrexham in pre-season, but they threw away two-goal leads in defeats by both Leeds and Monaco.
They averaged 60.6% possession over this small sample size - which is a 12.9% jump on Bournemouth's average possession under Iraola in the league last season.
With teams more likely to sit deep against Liverpool, having lots of possession is a newer challenge Iraola has to tackle.
And he has looked to do this while sticking to the intense and chaotic style that typified his previous sides.
- Follow Liverpool to get live score updates this season 
  - Published5 days ago
Since joining Liverpool, many of Iraola's tactics in possession look as they did last season.
Liverpool have looked to build up short at times with their goalkeeper, four defenders and one or two central midfielders deep.
Dominik Szoboszlai and Trey Nyoni, Liverpool's preferred deeper midfield duo in pre-season, drop to show for the ball, bouncing it towards wide players in space.
Iraola's sides have become known for fast and vertical counter-attacks but, with Liverpool looking to hold the ball more deliberately, these short passes in build-up are designed to entice opposition pressure before accelerating play.
Once a team have committed players to pressing Liverpool, Iraola's men look for forward passes readily - almost manufacturing their own counter-attacks.
If a team press immediately, Liverpool have been willing to skip short build-up play and go long from keepers Alisson or Giorgi Mamardashvili early.
By playing directly, even if Liverpool lose the initial duel, they are well placed to pounce upon second balls. They then look to attack the spaces that open up centrally against disorganised defences.
Many of Iraola's attacking principles resemble those of one of his long-time managerial inspirations, the former Leeds United boss Marcelo Bielsa.
The Argentine coached Iraola at Athletic Club between 2011 and 2013 and, speaking to Sky Sports in 2023, the Liverpool boss acknowledged this influence.
"I use a lot of exercises from Marcelo that I learned from him, especially with the ball," Iraola said.
"Offensively, his teams are very dynamic, willing to make all the runs to the space, he is ready to accept this kind of disorder offensively."
Like Bielsa's sides, Iraola already has the Reds playing in a busy manner. When attacking, it is rare to see Liverpool's players filling specific areas in a rigid style.
Another tactic Bielsa leans on is the use of wide pairings or trios to break teams down. Iraola experienced this at first hand when playing as a right-back for him.
The full-back and winger would regularly combine on the outside, but the relationship was never as simple as one holding the width and the other supporting underneath statically.
Bielsa, like Iraola now, encouraged players to change their positions in relation to each other.
The winger could come inside, opening the outside lane for the full-back, while a midfielder would move towards the pair to create a third passing option.
On other occasions, the full-back could move inside himself, allowing the winger to remain high and wide.
Liverpool are already showing similar patterns under Iraola, especially on the left, where full-backs have pushed into the final third alongside Rio Ngumoha or Cody Gakpo on the left wing.
Florian Wirtz, playing primarily as Liverpool's number 10 under Iraola, has drifted to that flank to provide a third option capable of playing centrally, deep or out wide.
The rotations of these wide triangles make it hard for opponents to know who they should be picking up.
By simplifying the attacking game into two-v-two or three-v-three situations, Liverpool are hoping to have a repeatable and dynamic solution, resulting in crosses from dangerous positions close to goal.
1 of 3
As exciting as this style of play can appear, it does leave Liverpool very top-heavy.
In the opening games, we have seen both full-backs join the attack alongside two of the midfield three and the front three.
This can result in situations that leave only the two centre-backs and one holding midfielder positioned behind the ball, leaving Liverpool vulnerable to counter-attacks.
Interestingly, Slot’s Liverpool were noticeably vulnerable against fast counter-attacks last season too.
Iraola has spoken about the need for more control while retaining the chaos that makes his team's attacks so effective, so he may decide to leave additional players behind the ball as the season progresses.
However, based off his previous principles and his managerial references, this feels less likely - with the Basque coach often encouraging six or seven players to push forward, leaving three or four players back when in attack.
The hope is to stop counter-attacks being conceded at source through intense counter-presses, something that is helped by attacking down the sides and with extra bodies nearby to apply pressure.
This is easier said than done at this early stage.
Indeed, Iraola reflected on the loss to Monaco, saying his side "can't sustain the level we want, we have work to do", referring to the dropped leads in second halves, caused by a lack of depth, a drop-off in physicality, and a press that hasn't yet been perfected.
Throughout pre-season, we have also seen Iraola's trademark high press. What stands out is the roles Liverpool's players are taking up and what that tells us about how he wants his side to defend.
Szoboszlai played across the front line, midfield and even at right-back last season, but Iraola has mainly used him as the second central midfielder - a crucial role defensively.
Liverpool have often pressed in a 4-4-2 diamond shape, initially encouraging opponents to play short before launching more aggressive pressing sequences, often funnelling the ball centrally before trying to win it back.
One principle carried over from Iraola's Bournemouth side is looking to keep a spare defender against the opposition attack. If an opponent leaves three forwards high, Liverpool will commonly opt to keep four defenders back.
That leaves one fewer player higher up the pitch, so Liverpool have to compensate through intensity and intelligent covering.
When one player leaves his opponent to press somebody else, team-mates behind him have to recognise the movement and cover the player left free.
This makes Szoboszlai's midfield role particularly important. When he jumps forward to press, the holding midfielder and defensive line have to react behind him or gaps can quickly appear.
"He is very good," the Hungary captain has said of his new manager. "The intensity we need is here now, what we have been missing is back."
Szoboszlai's physicality allows him to cover the ground needed to make Liverpool's press feel numerically equal, while his judgement of when to step forward has helped the Reds start to implement Iraola's defensive ideas quickly.
1 of 3
Four pre-season games is a very small sample, but Iraola's stamp on Liverpool is already clear to see, featuring many of the same instructions that defined his Bournemouth side.
Those ideas have been proven to work - but how he balances the chaos and speed we've come to know his sides for, with a squad lacking depth and who are expected to dominate the ball for longer periods, is likely to shape his first season.

title: Nigeria eliminated as Cameroon, Malawi reach WAFCON semis and World Cup

Nigeria eliminated as Cameroon, Malawi reach WAFCON semis and World Cup
Outsiders Malawi qualify for their first FIFA World Cup, while defending champions Nigeria are eliminated by Cameroon.
Rank outsiders Malawi qualified for the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) semifinals and the FIFA World Cup by coming from behind to beat Ghana 2-1 in Morocco on Sunday.
Trailing after just seven minutes when Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah volleyed Ghana into the lead, Malawi levelled five minutes later as a Temwa Chawinga shot was deflected into the net.
